World.title: Pittsburgh doctor stabbed to death after intruder allegedly attacks him, wife as they slept: police
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A Pittsburgh children's hospital doctor was stabbed to death and his wife critically injured after a man allegedly entered their home and attacked the couple as they slept early Thursday, police said.

Dr. Idris Evans, 46, was killed in the attack at his home in Edgewood, Pennsylvania, according to the Allegheny County Police Department.

His wife remained in critical but stable condition Thursday, police told Fox News Digital.

County 9-1-1 received a report of a stabbing in the 100 block of Linden Avenue at 12:31 a.m. First responders found Evans and his wife suffering from multiple stab wounds, police said.

ACTIVIST TIED TO OPRAH, BIDEN STABBED, AND TEACHER MOM SLAIN IN AMBUSH IN QUIET NEIGHBORHOOD

Evans was taken to an area hospital, where he was pronounced dead. His wife was also transported to a hospital.

Police identified 32-year-old Elijah Hemingway of Pittsburgh as the suspect.

Detectives determined through witness interviews that Hemingway allegedly entered the home and attacked Evans and his wife while they were sleeping, according to police.

Evans' wife told investigators that they awoke to a man attacking them in bed with a kitchen knife, according to court documents obtained by KDKA reported. She said the attacker was wearing only underwear and uttered about "being God," the outlet reported.

MACHETE-WIELDING SUSPECT CLAIMING TO BE 'LUCIFER' SHOT BY POLICE AFTER ALLEGEDLY STABBING 3 AT TRANSIT HUB

During the attack, Evans' wife yelled for the couple's children, ages 8 and 12, to get out of the house and go to a neighbor's home, according to KDKA.

She also told investigators that Evans called the attacker "Elijah," as though he knew him, according to the outlet.

"We do not know if there was any pre-existing relationship," Allegheny County Assistant Superintendent Victor Joseph said, according to KDKA. "The woman did not know this male. We are trying to determine if the two males knew each other."

A K-9 unit from the Monroeville Police Department searching the area found Hemingway behind a nearby home with cuts to his hand, according to county police. Hemingway remained hospitalized Thursday pending transfer to the Allegheny County Jail, police told Fox News Digital.

Hemingway faces charges including criminal homicide, aggravated assault, burglary and criminal trespass, police said. Police told Fox News Digital there were no updates to the charges Thursday.

NORTH CAROLINA MAN BROKE INTO EX'S HOME, FATALLY STABBED HIS 5-YEAR-OLD SON BEFORE GOING TO TACO BELL: POLICE

Investigators have not announced a motive. Police told Fox News Digital that both a possible motive and whether Hemingway and Evans knew each other remained part of the ongoing investigation.

Evans was medical director of the Pediatric Critical Care Transport Team at UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh and an assistant professor of critical care medicine at the University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine, according to his university profile.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"The UPMC and University of Pittsburgh community is deeply saddened by the tragic loss of Dr. Idris Evans, a pediatric critical care physician at UPMC Children’s Hospital of Pittsburgh and an assistant professor of critical care medicine at the University of Pittsburgh," a UPMC spokesperson told Fox News Digital in a statement.

"Dr. Evans was a dedicated caregiver and valued member of our hospital and university communities. Our thoughts are with his family, loved ones, and colleagues during this difficult time. We ask that their privacy be respected."

World.title: New Jersey Gov Mikie Sherrill calls on lieutenant governor to resign after sexual harassment investigation
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill called on handpicked Lt. Gov. Dale Caldwell to resign by Friday after an independent investigation substantiated sexual harassment and two ethics violations.

The investigation found Caldwell told a female staffer that "you young women are looking for young sperm" after she told him her younger friend was not interested in a romantic relationship with him.

Investigators concluded the sexually charged remark constituted sexual harassment and said Caldwell's denial that he made the comment was not credible.

The staffer said she subsequently attempted to distance herself from Caldwell at work and avoid traveling with him when possible.

REPUBLICANS TIGHTEN SCREWS ON SHERRILL AS NONCITIZEN VOTER PROBE ENTERS NEW PHASE

"I’m calling for his resignation and giving him until tomorrow to do so," Sherrill said Thursday, calling the substantiated sexual harassment finding "extremely troubling."

The report also substantiated two ethics violations, finding Caldwell brought personal guests to ticketed events without advance ethics clearance or payment and repeatedly attempted to secure a promotion for a state employee with whom he had a romantic relationship.

Investigators found Caldwell continued bringing unpaid guests to events despite repeated training and warnings, including on May 23, one day after he was formally notified of the investigation.

SHERRILL ESCALATES TRUMP FIGHT OVER VOTER FIASCO DAY AFTER MULLIN PRAISES NJ COOPERATION

Four days after receiving notice of the investigation, Caldwell also used his state email account to recommend his romantic partner for a leadership position in another executive branch department, referring to her as "my friend" and forwarding her resume and letter of interest. Investigators said Caldwell did not disclose their romantic relationship while advocating for her promotion.

Caldwell denied wrongdoing in a May response to investigators, calling the allegations false and misleading and saying he believed the facts would exonerate him. He denied hitting on or asking women out while conducting official business.

Fox News Digital reached out to Caldwell for comment on the report and Sherrill's resignation demand.

Sherrill said the violations reflected "a pattern of behavior" that persisted despite warnings and training.

"The lieutenant governor’s resignation is necessary and in the best interest of New Jersey residents," the Democrat said.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Sherrill also took aim at President Donald Trump in announcing her decision, saying the president "continues to undermine confidence in public service at the federal level" and that she would not accept "a culture that sweeps misconduct under the rug" in New Jersey.

The investigation began after the state's chief ethics officer received an anonymous complaint in May alleging inappropriate behavior toward women and ethics violations. Caldwell was formally notified of the investigation May 22.

World.title: FBI says source of its jobs portal breach still unknown as hackers allege employee data compromised
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The FBI is working to determine whether a breach involving its jobs website originated within the bureau or through a third-party provider after a criminal hacking group claimed it obtained FBI employees’ personal information.

"The FBI is aware of a cyber-criminal enterprise group claiming a compromise of the FBIJobs.gov portal and alleged impact to FBI employee personally identifiable information (PII)," the organization wrote in an X post Thursday.

"While the point of breach is still undetermined — whether a third-party or the FBI’s enterprise — we are actively and aggressively investigating this matter and working closely with those third-party providers that support FBIJobs.gov to mitigate any and all risk."

Jason Pack, CEO of Media Rep Global Strategies and a retired FBI supervisory special agent, said the distinction between a personnel data breach and access to the FBI’s classified systems is critical as investigators determine the scope of the incident.

FBI INVESTIGATES AFTER SHINYHUNTERS HACKERS CLAIM THEFT OF AGENTS' PERSONAL DATA

"There is a meaningful difference between somebody obtaining personnel information and somebody gaining access to classified investigative systems," he told Fox News Digital. "Based on what we know right now, there is no indication they have the keys to the kingdom."

ShinyHunters, a criminal hacking and extortion group, has taken responsibility for the breach and said it stole information belonging to nearly all FBI agents and people who applied to work for the bureau, Reuters previously reported.

A sample of data shared with Reuters contained agents’ names, home addresses, Social Security numbers, assignments and, in some cases, names of family members, according to the outlet.

DMV BREACH CONFIRMED AS HACKERS CLAIM 200,000 RECORDS STOLEN

Pack said combining personal information with information about an FBI employee's work could create additional security risks.

"If an adversary knows who somebody is, where they work and what they do, they can build a much more believable scam around that person," he said.

Pack said assignment information could also carry counterintelligence implications if it falls into the hands of a foreign intelligence service.

"There is also a counterintelligence concern. If a foreign intelligence service can associate particular people with certain assignments, it can help them identify individuals they may want to learn more about, approach or potentially assess for recruitment," he added.

"That does not mean that is happening here. It simply explains why assignment information can have value to an adversary."

CHINA-LINKED HACKERS INFILTRATED US GOVERNMENT NETWORKS BEFORE FBI TAKEDOWN

Pack stressed that the hackers’ claims remain separate from what the FBI has confirmed, and said the bureau still needs to determine what information was accessed, how the breach occurred and who may have been affected.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"The danger from stolen personal information does not necessarily end when the computer vulnerability is fixed," he said. "Criminals may hold onto that information and use it weeks or months later."

The FBI said it is working with third-party providers supporting FBIJobs.gov as investigators seek to determine the source of the breach and mitigate potential risks.

World.title: Mamdani-backed socialist arrested at anti-Netanyahu protest outside UN
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Darializa Avila Chevalier, a socialist House candidate in New York, was arrested Thursday while protesting Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's visit to New York City during the United Nation's General Assembly meeting, according to photos shared on social media by her campaign and public media reports.

Avila Chevalier, the Democratic nominee for New York's 13th Congressional District, was among dozens of demonstrators taken into custody after protesters blocked a roadway near the United Nations General Assembly meeting Thursday ahead of Netanyahu's address at the event.

"Darializa was just arrested while peacefully protesting Netanyahu's speech at the United Nations," a Thursday afternoon post from the candidate's social media account said.

"Our government has unlimited funds to arm a genocide against Palestinians but tells us there's nothing left to feed and house our own people. Stop arming Israel!"

ISRAEL'S AMBASSADOR SAYS NYC’S MAMDANI IS ‘SOWING CHAOS’ AHEAD OF NETANYAHU’S UN APPEARANCE

The demonstration Avila Chevalier was reportedly arrested at drew around 250 protesters to the corner of 1st Avenue and 39th Street in Manhattan, according to City & State New York. Police began making arrests after protesters sitting in the roadway refused to move.

Avila Chevalier defended her participation following the arrest.

"Netanyahu belongs at the Hague, not in the streets of New York City, and certainly not addressing the United Nations General Assembly," she said in a statement reported by Bloomberg.

Avila Chevalier was not the only New York political figure taken into custody. City Council members Chi Ossé and Alexa Avilés were also arrested during the demonstration, according to City & State, while the Daily Mail reported actress Susan Sarandon was among those detained at the protest.

Outlets reported that roughly 80 to 100 protesters who refused orders and remained at the demonstration were arrested.

RISING SOCIALIST STARS ON TRACK TO CONGRESS: WHO ARE DARIALIZA AVILA CHEVALIER, BRAD LANDER AND CLAIRE VALDEZ?

Avila Chevalier, 32, pulled off a major Democratic primary upset in June when she defeated five-term Democratic incumbent Rep. Adriano Espaillat in the heavily Democratic 13th District, which covers Upper Manhattan and parts of the Bronx.

Fox News Digital previously reported that New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani endorsed Avila Chevalier in late May during an appearance on MS NOW, praising her commitment to working-class New Yorkers and saying he looked forward to fighting alongside her for their shared affordability agenda.

She is a member of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) and received backing from the group's New York City chapter during her congressional campaign.

Avila Chevalier has been a prominent pro-Palestinian activist as well, with Fox News Digital previously reporting on how she led anti-Israel protests at Columbia University and said she helped launch Columbia University Apartheid Divest's (CUAD) boycott, divestment and sanctions campaign. CUAD later drew scrutiny for social media posts, including "Death to America" and a call for the "eradication of Western civilization."

World.title: JJ Redick takes shot at LeBron James, promises starters will not be all 'white guys' in odd presser
World.content:
You can put a podcaster in the head coach's chair, but you still end up with a podcaster.

Los Angeles Lakers coach JJ Redick proved as much during his annual news conference Thursday, giving answers better suited for the Twitter timeline than a head coach's seat.

First, Redick offered a shady response about the team gelling after superstar LeBron James departed.

LEBRON JAMES TELLS LOS ANGELES LAKERS HE WILL LEAVE IN FREE AGENCY AFTER EIGHT SEASONS: REPORT

He pointedly noted that this roster has a clearer identity than past squads led by James, his former podcast co-host.

"I think we’ve always tried to give our players clearly defined roles, and I think with this group, [it’s] probably the first time in my three years here that I feel like the pieces actually fit together," Redick said. "And so those roles probably get even more crystallized."

Since LeBron’s departure, a running joke has taken over Lakers fandom.

"Snowtime" has trended across social media as the tongue-in-cheek nickname for the Lakers' projected core of Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler — with nods to depth pieces like Dalton Knecht and Maxi Kleber.

STEPHEN A SMITH SHOWS HIS PRIVILEGE BY MOCKING LAKERS' ROSTER FOR HAVING TOO MANY 'WHITE DUDES'

Because the team's projected top talent isn't Black, the online gag caught fire, and Redick awkwardly addressed it with a questionable remark about his starting unit.

Without much context, Redick said he was confident two positions in his lineup would "not be white."

"I'm pretty confident in three of the spots," Redick said. "The other two spots will not be two white guys."

It was a sarcastic wink to the online crowd, and a cheap internet laugh at best.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Redick now enters his third season at the helm in Los Angeles. His squad was swept in the Western Conference Semifinals by OKC last spring, following a first-round exit against the Minnesota Timberwolves in his inaugural season.

Before taking the bench, Redick spent 15 years as an NBA sharpshooter. In 2024, he teamed up with LeBron James to co-host "Mind the Game," a wine-drinking, X's-and-O's basketball podcast.

PHILADELPHIA ATHLETES, INCLUDING NEW TEAMMATES, REACT TO LEBRON JAMES JOINING 76ERS: 'WELCOME TO THE CITY'

By July 2026, after two seasons together in LA, the dynamic completely shifted when LeBron packed his bags for Philly, leaving Redick to run the show solo.

World.title: Trump rolls out red carpets for Xi, though he has portrayed China as a global menace
World.content:
WASHINGTON — He has accused China of hacking America’s elections and plundering its wealth, yet President Donald Trump has showered the visiting Chinese leader, Xi Jinping, with tributes and affection during their summit meeting this week at the White House.

Trump met his Chinese counterpart on the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland, outside Washington on Wednesday rather than wait back at the White House for an official greeting. It’s the first time he has ever shown a visiting world leader that courtesy.

Trump rolled out a red carpet not once but twice for Xi. The leaders walked side by side down a 100-foot-long red carpet after Xi’s Air China plane landed at Andrews. Another red carpet was laid out Thursday morning when Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, arrived at the White House for the summit’s first full day.

President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump welcome Chinese leader Xi Jinping and China's First Lady Peng Liyuan at the White House ahead of a state dinner on Thursday. Saul Loeb / AFP via Getty Images

In the evening, Trump feted Xi at a state dinner whose menu included sesame-crusted sea bass and braised bok choy, followed by a dessert of vanilla crémeux and honey ice cream.

“As the leaders of our two nations, President Xi and I both understand that we represent different systems, but the ties between our people endure, and we’ve never gotten along better since the first trade ships from New York left the harbor to arrive on the banks of the Pearl River,” Trump said at the dinner.

He gave his guest a statue of a bald eagle as a gift.

All the pomp and ceremony might appear unusual given Trump’s past complaints that China has meddled in elections and exploited the U.S. through trade. Just two months ago, Trump gave a rare primetime speech asserting that China interfered in the 2020 election, which he lost to Joe Biden.

But Trump, who has long believed that personal relationships are key to managing geopolitical tensions, has set out to charm the Chinese leader.

A bald eagle statue is presented as a gift to Xi during the state dinner in the East Room of the White House. Kevin Dietsch / Getty Images

“From the time of my first election in 2016, President Xi and I have forged a friendship — a truly great friendship, actually — built on mutual respect and the vital interests of our people,” Trump said Thursday morning in joint public statements he and Xi made before they held a private meeting in the Oval Office.

Xi struck a cordial tone in his remarks, saying he and Trump have developed a “personal rapport and stayed in touch.”

He also made an announcement certain to delight American children and anyone who has ever logged on to a panda-cam feed for a respite from life’s pressures: China will soon send two giant pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shang, to the Atlanta zoo, Xi said.

In an unusual rebuke from a member of Trump’s own party, Sen. Roger Wicker, R-Miss., chairman of the Armed Services Committee, said Wednesday in a speech on the Senate floor that, “quite frankly, had the White House asked me for advice, I would have suggested the president not invite Xi Jinping to Washington for such a lavish welcome here in the United States of America, based on all of the troubling issues we have with President Xi and the Chinese Communist Party.”

01:22 President Trump in landmark meeting with China’s leader 00:00 00:00

China may also have aided Iran in the war with the U.S. An F-15 fighter jet that was shot down over Iran in April was most likely hit by a Chinese-made shoulder-launched missile, three people familiar with the matter told NBC News. And in the early days of the seven-month-old conflict, China may have given Iran radar capabilities to help spot stealth aircraft, according to one of the people and a U.S. official with knowledge of the matter.

Honoring the leader of the world’s largest communist country may also undercut an argument Trump has made to discredit Democrats in the midterm elections. He has warned repeatedly that Democratic candidates would steer the U.S. in a communist direction if they are elected.

Sen. Lisa Murkowski, R-Alaska, told NBC News on Thursday, “I personally look at the red-carpet treatment and thought it was a little bit over the top.”

Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., said in an interview that while he didn’t mind seeing Xi thrown a dinner, “I don’t think the president ought to believe his bull----.”

After the U.S. and Israel launched attacks on Iran on Feb. 28, the Iranian regime exerted a chokehold over the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial shipping lane for oil supplies.

Xi “could open up that strait with a phone call, and in a myriad of ways, he is helping Iran with military equipment, intelligence,” Kennedy said. “The guy learned to lie before he learned to talk.”

Kevin Dietsch / Getty Images

China, which has criticized the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran and called for diplomatic negotiations, denies supplying Iran with weapons or military equipment.

No substantive breakthroughs are expected at the summit, foreign policy experts said. The two presidents were set to discuss trade, the Iran war and artificial intelligence, among other issues that have divided the U.S. and China. Trump entered the summit in a weakened posture, experts said, vexed by the prolonged Iran war and looming midterm congressional elections in which his party could lose its slim majority. He lacks the leverage needed to wring concessions from China, experts said.

Mark Montgomery, a retired Navy admiral, said at a pre-summit event hosted by the FDD think tank: “We have a president entering this playing a weak hand. I’m not 100% sure President Trump knows he’s playing a weak hand. I am 100% sure that leader Xi knows Trump is playing a weak hand.”

One area of cooperation might be the creation of a hotline that the U.S. and China could use to cope with an emergency arising from rapidly evolving AI technology, Secretary of State Marco Rubio suggested in an interview on “Fox & Friends” this week.

“It’s not a bad idea; it’s one that we’ll explore with the Chinese, among others,” Rubio said.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, left, and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg at the state dinner on Thursday. Brendan Smialowski / AFP via Getty Images

Along with closed-door meetings, Trump made a point to show off his prized White House projects. He took Xi outside to see the helipad he built on the South Lawn. Both men pointed down at the granite base.

When the leaders passed the press corps at one point, Trump said, “We had a great meeting.” He said Xi was “an expert on stone, aside from many other things, and he loves good granite.”

Xi said nothing.

Walking with Xi along the West Wing Colonnade, Trump pointed to his “Presidential Walk of Fame” — pictures and biographical accounts of former presidents. He paused at the portrait of Biden, showing how he has mocked Biden by referring to him as “Autopen,” the device that presidents have used when they don’t have time to sign their own names to documents. A video snippet released by the White House shows the two presidents chuckling at the picture of Biden, with Trump giving Xi a friendly pat on the arm.

Confronting Xi in the moment may prove difficult for Trump. Xi is president for life; Trump is a president at risk of losing his governing majority in Congress. His approval rating has hit a second-term low.

President Donald Trump speaks with Chinese President Xi Jinping through interpreters during the state dinner. Kevin Dietsch / Getty Images

One source of Xi’s leverage is his hold over rare earth materials, which are used in high-tech manufacturing. Last year, Trump slapped China with steep tariffs, igniting a trade war. Trump has long complained that China’s trade policies have bled the U.S. of wealth.

A statement from the White House in April 2025, tied to Trump’s “Liberation Day” tariffs, said Chinese practices “have given China global dominance in key manufacturing industries, decimating U.S. industry.”

But China’s command of rare earth supplies has proved an effective countermeasure, a resource the Trump administration can’t afford to lose. The two sides agreed to a trade truce last year, and on Wednesday they agreed to extend it two months, from Nov. 10 to Jan. 10.

Viewers who wanted to watch the summit live faced unusual difficulties following a media ban that Trump imposed last week. He barred CNN, MS NOW and Politico from entering the White House grounds, prompting them to sue to regain access.

CNN is part of the five-network press “pool” that provides real-time coverage of the president’s public events. In solidarity with CNN and the other outlets that were banned, the other networks opted to suspend video pool coverage of Trump.

Confusion reigned in the hours before Xi arrived. ABC News had been scheduled to provide the pooled video feed. A White House official hurriedly approached a network journalist and asked where the camera was. Absent any clarity over when the banned outlets’ access would be restored, ABC declined to record.

Trump took notice that TV coverage had thinned. He wrote on social media that CNN and MS NOW “refused to cover one of the Biggest and Most Beautiful Events to take place in many years, the arrival at the White House of the Highly Respected President of China, Xi Jinping, and his beautiful wife, Madam Peng.”

Peng Liyuan and Melania Trump arrive for the state dinner. Kevin Dietsch / Getty Images

Journalists from both CNN and MS NOW were physically unable to cover Xi’s arrival at the White House. Though a federal judge had ruled overnight that their access must be restored, they were still barred from entering the White House until about two hours after Xi showed up.

During a photo spray with Xi later in the day, Trump joked that China had the friendliest press corps, according to a press pool report.

A Reporters Without Borders survey of press freedoms worldwide ranked China 178th out of 180 countries, sandwiched between North Korea and Iran.

World.title: It’s cute. It’s cuddly. And it wants all your data.
World.content:
Meta hopes its new AI agent will win people over by being cute.

Muse, the tech giant’s cuddly, doll-like AI agent, shot to the top of the Apple App Store charts after it was featured this week at the company’s Meta Connect conference.

The company is touting the tool, designed to help people with their everyday tasks, as an AI agent “built for everyone,” including those who lack experience with technology.

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said the default Muse avatar, which is cream-colored and has beady black eyes and an upward smile, is named “Jolly,” for its “jolly and completely customizable character and personality.”

Muse is being launched as tech companies seek to make their AI-powered products more palatable to humans, often by giving them cute, almost petlike appearances, voices and personalities. Experts have said design choices that humanize technology may become more common as robot-human interaction grows more prevalent in everyday spaces, as cuteness evokes “deep-seated biological responses” in people.

“It was only about six months ago that having a personal agent running on your own computer was the sign of someone who is completely AI-pilled and thinking nonstop about agents,” Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, said Wednesday. “But for that small group of nerds ... it looked like the beginning of personal superintelligence. And today with Muse, we’ve brought that magic to everyone.”

Mark Zuckerberg's Muse AI Agent, Agrippa. Meta

Muse agents can take on a variety of appearances, with users able to customize everything from their names to their attire. Zuckerberg’s agent, which wears a toga and a wreath around its head, is named Agrippa, after the Roman general and statesman.

During the event, Zuckerberg also teased what he calls the “Muse charm,” a small handheld device that can activate the agent on the go. He raised the keychain charm onstage at Meta Connect in Menlo Park, California, showing off what looks like a blend of a Labubu and a Tamagotchi.

“Talking to your Muse is often the fastest way to get things done, and it is also just really fun and cute,” he said, saying he used Agrippa to come up with a baking recipe and order ingredients for him and his daughter.

Muse is also being integrated directly into Meta’s expanding lineup of AI-powered glasses, which have been criticized over fears of casual surveillance. Zuckerberg has told NBC News that Meta will continue to bolster privacy safeguards for its smart glasses.

Zuckerberg said every Muse agent has its own private and secure computer called Muse Secure VM, a dedicated secure computer that houses both the agent and the user’s personal data. Down the line, he said, Meta plans to release Muse Confidential VM “so that even Meta won’t be able to see that information.”

“In the coming years, I expect that Muse is going to grow into the personal superintelligence that billions of people around the world are going to use to accomplish their goals and improve their lives,” he said.

Online, the reaction has been mixed.

Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, posted a flurry of memes inserting Muse into moments from movies, shows and historical events.

Some followed his lead by making their own avatars and sharing screenshots on social media.

Others, however, expressed skepticism, citing security concerns.

“Am I the only one who doesn’t want to let meta have access to my whole life?” a user posted.

“We are going to need some tight defenses and 3rd party testing of these platforms... like all software products,” entrepreneur and angel investor Jason Calacanis wrote.

Zuckerberg has continued to be bullish on AI despite recent calls from tech executives and government officials to pump the brakes on AI development amid surging fears about the existential risk the technology poses.

He shared his thoughts recently on X, saying market forces should be enough to keep AI companies in line.

“My view is that trust and alignment are quickly becoming the most important capabilities that will differentiate agents and models. Any lab that doesn’t focus on alignment will fall behind,” he wrote, adding: “Meta delayed shipping Muse for several months to focus on safety and security. We didn’t call for everyone else to do this before we would.”

World.title: Error leads to backlog of tens of thousands of voter registration applications in Texas
World.content:
Texas officials sent tens of thousands of delayed voter registration applications to county election officials this week after discovering an error, sparking a scramble to process them weeks out from the midterms.

The Texas secretary of state’s office told election officials last week that a problem with the Department of Public Safety’s system had been uncovered: Certain incomplete voter registration applications that were missing some information were not sent on to election officials, potentially leaving Texans unregistered or with out-of-date voter files. The nonprofit news outlet Votebeat was the first to report the problem.

State officials started transmitting the records on Tuesday. It’s unclear how many voters were affected, but large counties have reported tens of thousands of registration applications and updates that election officials must process in the less than a month before early voting begins on Oct. 19. And more applications are sure to pour in ahead of the Oct. 5 deadline to register to vote in Texas.

Voters line up in Houston on March 3, 2026. Ronaldo Schemidt / AFP via Getty Images

The state’s fourth-most populous county, Bexar, received more than 45,000 voter registration forms from DPS, and the fifth-most populous, Travis County, received more than 35,000.

“While that number may seem high, the Elections team is already hard at work reviewing every application and will be extending hours to make sure all records are updated well before early voting begins,” Bexar County Elections Administrator Michele Carew said in a statement.

Chris McGinn, the executive director of the Texas Association of County Election Officials, said he expected populous urban areas will be hit hardest, because there are more voter registrations to process and people in cities tend to move more often.

“There’s going to be a lot of counties that are paying a lot of overtime,” he said, speaking in a press briefing organized by the nonpartisan Center for Election Innovation and Research.

McGinn said some of the records may be duplicative — people may check the box to register to vote when they update their driver’s license, for instance — but still need time and attention from election officials.

Alicia Pierce, a spokesperson for the Texas secretary of state’s office, said a voter who does not appear on the state’s rolls but believes they registered to vote can cast a provisional ballot, and election officials can later search DPS records.

Texas is hosting several competitive statewide elections this fall. Democratic state Rep. James Talarico is facing off against Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton for a U.S. Senate seat. And Democratic state Rep. Gina Hinojosa is challenging GOP Gov. Greg Abbott.

In a statement, Talarico called the error “unacceptable” and urged Texans to check their voter registration online.

“Less than two weeks before the voter registration deadline, thousands of Texans are now in the dark about their voter registration status — even more aren’t aware of this error at all,” Talarico said. “This is what a broken, corrupt political system looks like: Texans follow the rules, register to vote before the deadline, and still risk losing their God-given right to the ballot box because their government failed to do its job.”

McGinn said voters might be better off calling their local registrar’s office. Texas’ online system has reportedly had problems this year, with some registrations inaccurately showing up as inactive.

World.title: Ole Miss identifies 2 students found dead in cases that raise kratom concerns
World.content:
The University of Mississippi said Thursday that undergraduate students from Colorado and Georgia died this week in cases that sparked renewed concerns about kratom.

Aidan Hamilton, 18, a freshman from Englewood, Colorado, and Robert Strang, 20, a junior from Atlanta, were found dead in separate locations this week, Ole Miss said.

Robert Strang. Courtesy Strang family

Both students were discovered Monday, one on campus and the other in the city of Oxford, authorities have said. Packaged kratom was found during each of the death investigations, but no definitive link has been made between kratom and the deaths, officials said.

Kratom is an herb with opioidlike effects sometimes sold at gas stations or online. It has gained popularity in the U.S. as an unapproved treatment for pain, anxiety and drug dependence. Kratom can be stimulating or sedating, depending on the dosage taken, according to the Drug Enforcement Administration.

“We are heartbroken by the loss of our dear son, Robert, and are trying to process this unimaginable loss,” the Strang family said in a statement. “We are deeply grateful for the incredible outpouring of love, prayers and support by so many beloved friends and family. Their kindness has meant more to our family than we can ever express.”

“As we grieve and focus on our family, we ask for privacy, understanding and compassion in the days ahead,” the statement said.

The Hamilton family said Aidan Hamilton was “a bright, wonderful young man who was taken too soon.”

“He is greatly missed. We thank everyone for their prayers and support and ask that you respect our family’s privacy during this time of great loss,” the family said in a statement.

Shawnboda Mead, the university’s vice chancellor for student affairs, cautioned the campus community about misinformation.

“We know there is heightened media attention and that you may be eager for answers. We also recognize that inaccurate information is being shared by individuals who do not have access to the facts,” Mead said in a statement.

“We can all help by not repeating information that has not been officially confirmed and by avoiding public speculation about what happened or why, especially as the causes of the two deaths are still under investigation.”

Phi Delta Theta fraternity said Strang was a member.

“Out of respect for Robert, his family, and those closest to him, the Fraternity has refrained from public comment until his name was publicly released,” it said in a statement Thursday.

“The loss of two young lives is a profound tragedy,” it said. “Phi Delta Theta joins the University of Mississippi and the broader Ole Miss community in mourning Robert and Aidan Hamilton and extending our deepest sympathies to their families, friends, chapter brothers, classmates, and all those who knew and loved them.”

World.title: The U.S. economy before and after the Iran war, in five charts
World.content:
On Feb. 27, the day before the United States and Israel attacked Iran, the American economy was on a steady course to lower inflation and attain greater buying power. Gas was cheap and interest rates were coming down.

Today, none of those things are true anymore. When it comes to the U.S. economy, there’s before the Iran war — and since.

Despite assurances from President Donald Trump as early as March that the war would prove a “short-term excursion,” the conflict is about to round its seventh month. On Tuesday, Trump suggested that a deal could arrive after November’s midterm elections.

The morass has short-circuited Trump’s ability to tout other, more positive economic developments during his second term. The Census Bureau reported last week that the median U.S. household income hit an all-time high in 2025, while the percentage of people in the U.S. living in poverty fell to its lowest level on record. The stock market has done well this year, and the unemployment rate remains low.

Yet, on balance, the negative news has served to obscure the good, both for individual consumers and the nation at large. Before the war, gas prices were just under $3 a gallon. Today they’re at approximately $4.50 on average. Diesel prices went from an average of $3.75 on Feb. 28 to an all-time high of more than $6.50 on Tuesday.

This has caused a domino effect in which inflation rose, then borrowing costs, then mortgage rates.

Surveys of consumer sentiment and presidential approval polls continue to drift lower even as household spending on extras such as travel and dining out remains steady. In March, 35% of respondents to an NBC News poll said Trump had helped the economy. By September, that figure had declined to just 26%.

The White House defended the president’s record in a statement to NBC News.

“President Trump has always been clear about temporary disruptions as a result of the Iran conflict, but the Trump administration has remained laser-focused delivering on the President’s long-term economic agenda on the home front,” White House spokesman Kush Desai said in a statement.

The changes wrought by the war are nevertheless unmistakable. With less than six weeks until the midterm elections, the charts below offer the clearest picture yet of the challenge the White House faces as it works to retain Republican control of Congress.

Gas and diesel prices

The major reason for inflation’s run-up has been higher energy prices, especially fuel. Prior to the war’s launch, average gas prices stood at just under $3 a gallon, while diesel prices were less than $4 a gallon. Today, gas is nearly $4.50 — its highest ever for late September — and diesel prices continue to set records, most recently hitting $6.52.

World.title: Hurricane Nolo could cause "catastrophic" flooding in Hawaii, forecasters warn
World.content:
Hurricane Nolo is approaching Hawaii as a potential "catastrophic" rainmaker, the National Hurricane Center says.

It's threatening to dump up to 3 feet of rain on Hawaii's Big Island, enough to cause "catastrophic and life-threatening flash flooding," the center warns, and is expected to bring heavy rainfall to the Big Island for the next several days.

Nolo strengthened into a hurricane on Thursday over the Pacific Ocean after hitting tropical storm strength Wednesday.

Maps show Hurricane Nolo's path

Nolo had maximum sustained winds of 75 mph as of Thursday night local time — barely above the 74 mph need for a storm to be categorized as a hurricane on Saffir-Simpson scale. But the Miami-based hurricane center said "steady to rapid intensification" is expected and "Nolo is forecast to become a major hurricane by this weekend." Major hurricanes have winds of at least 111 mph.

Hurricane-force winds extended outward up to 30 miles from Nolo's core and tropical-storm-force winds extended outward up to 105 miles.

Nolo's center was some 435 miles south-southeast of Honolulu and 255 miles south of South Point, which is on the Big Island and is the southern-most point in the entire U.S. It was moving north-northeast at 5 mph.

Nolo is expected to approach the Big Island on Friday and Saturday, and its center is expected to skirt just south of it.

The projected path of Hurricane Nolo in the Pacific Ocean. Sept. 24, 2026. NOAA

The Big Island was under a hurricane watch and tropical storm warning, and a tropical storm watch was in effect for Maui County.

"Tropical storm conditions are expected to begin by late Friday in the warning area, with hurricane conditions possible by

early Saturday. Tropical storm conditions are possible in the tropical storm watch area beginning on Saturday," the center said.

Hurricane Nolo as seen from a satellite south of Hawaii early on Friday, eastern time. NOAA / National Hurricane Center

Nolo is expected to bring around 15 to 30 inches of rain to the eastern and southern portions of the Big Island, with up to 35 inches possible in some areas. That much rain could trigger "catastrophic life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain," the hurricane center warned.

The Big Island's western areas could see 5 to 8 inches of rain and 10 at most. For Maui, 4 to 8 inches are possible with as much as 15 in some spots. Those totals could also produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain, the center stressed. The rest of Hawaii is likely to get 1 to 3 inches and 6 at most, enough to set off isolated flooding.

Map shows the rain forecast through Tuesday morning, Sept. 29, for Hawaii. CBS News

All state parks on the Big Island will be closed Thursday, and all state parks on Maui will be closed Friday because of the storm, the state's Department of Land and Natural Resources said Thursday.

Map shows active tropical alerts for Hawaii as of Sept. 24, 2026. CBS News

Nolo formed as another storm, Hurricane Polo, continued to swirl in the Pacific, off Mexico's southwestern coast.

Map shows the Eastern Pacific tropical outlook. CBS News

The latest storms add to an unsually active season in the Pacific. Earlier this month, Hurricane Lowell brought damaging winds and heavy rain to the western Hawaiian islands of Kauai and Niihau, bringing down trees, damaging roads and knocking out power for thousands.

Last month, Hurricane Lala washed away about 100 homes, triggered landslides and caused widespread power outages as it brushed past Hawaii.

World.title: Hurricane Polo is a powerful Category 4 storm off Mexico. See its path.
World.content:
Hurricane Polo's intensity oscillated between Category 4 and Category 5 on Thursday as its path started moving away from Mexico's southwestern coast. The storm was expected to remain offshore, while its outer rainbands spread across southwestern Mexico, the U.S. National Hurricane Center said.

Some strengthening was expected early Friday morning, but Polo was expected to weaken beginning Friday night and into Saturday, the Miami-based center said. Polo's center was expected to begin moving away from the southwestern Mexico coastline, forecasters said.

Elsewhere in the Pacific, Nolo strengthened into a hurricane on Thursday as it barreled down on Hawaii's Big Island.

Maps show Hurricane Polo's path

As of Thursday night, Polo's core was about 195 miles off the coast of Manzanillo, a coastal city in the Mexican state of Colima.

Hurricane Polo's forecast path as of Thursday, Sept. 24, 2026. CBS News

It was sending hurricane-force winds outward up to 40 miles from its center and tropical storm-force winds some 125 miles out. Polo was heading northwest at 10 mph.

Polo was forecast to bring tropical storm conditions to parts of the coastline on Thursday. In some areas, heavy rainfall "may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain," the hurricane center warned.

Although the storm has remained far south of Baja California, the center said Polo could still impact the peninsula this weekend.

The Mexican government canceled all tropical storm warnings and watches associated with Polo late Thursday for southwestern Mexico. Tropical storm warnings are issued when forecasts indicate tropical storm conditions will develop in a particular area, while tropical storm watches are issued when those conditions are possible, but not imminent.

Parts of the states of Michoacán, Colima, Jalisco and Nayarit may still see 2 to 4 more inches of rain, with up to 6 additional inches possible in certain areas, the hurricane center said Thursday. Between 1 and 2 more inches of rain could also fall in coastal parts of Jalisco and Guerrero.

Along with rain, Polo was also expected to cause life-threatening surf conditions, including rip currents, along the southwestern Mexican coast and parts of Baja California. The surf conditions could also contribute to flooding.

Mexican leaders have ordered evacuations, opened shelters and deployed military troops to areas that could be affected by the storm.

Classes were suspended Thursday at schools across the city of Acapulco, along the coast of Guerrero, its municipal government announced. Shelters across the state remained open, and officials said they were coordinating with local and national authorities to prepare for additional impacts of the hurricane.

Michoacán authorities also canceled classes through Friday in municipalities along the coast, urging residents of those areas not to leave their homes unless it was essential.

Polo's extreme rapid intensification

Polo underwent what's called extreme rapid intensification, in which a storm's wind speeds increase by 58 mph or more over the course of 24 hours, between Monday and Tuesday.

Its intensification was dramatic even by those standards, with winds that skyrocketed from 45 mph early Monday morning to 150 mph at around the same time the following day. The hurricane center described its transformation as "truly remarkable."

Its maximum sustained winds climbed as high as 180 mph at one point, far exceeding the 157 mph threshold for Category 5, the strongest on the hurricane scale.

Polo's central pressure — an indicator of its strength and potential destructiveness — made it the second-strongest hurricane on record in the Eastern Pacific, behind 2015's Hurricane Patricia. The storm's wind speeds tied 2009's Hurricane Rick as the third-strongest on record for the region.

Unusually strong El Niño conditions this year have been amping up tropical cyclone activity in the Pacific, with warmer waters, moist air and less wind shear enabling storm formation.

World.title: Pittsburgh doctor attacked and killed while he slept, wife also stabbed
World.content:
A physician and medical director from UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh was killed in an overnight stabbing that also left his wife injured in his home in Edgewood Borough.

Dr. Idris Evans, 46, died after he and his wife were violently attacked while they slept in their home along Linden Avenue early Thursday, police said. A suspect has been taken into custody.

According to court paperwork, Evans' wife told police that they awoke to a man attacking them in bed with a kitchen knife. She said he was wearing only underwear and uttered about "being God," the report said.

At some point during the attack she yelled for their children, 8 and 12 years old, to get out of the house and go to a neighbor's.

She told police that her husband called their attacker by the name "Elijah," as if he knew him.

Dr. Idris Evans, a physician from UPMC Children's Hospital in Pittsburgh, was killed in a stabbing in Edgewood Borough. UPMC

The Allegheny County Police Department said they were called to the scene around 12:30 a.m.

Responding officers found a man and woman suffering from stab wounds. Both individuals were taken to the hospital in critical condition, but Evans later died.

"It was a very violent scene," said Allegheny County Assistant Superintendent Victor Joseph. "The bedroom furniture was broken, mirrors broken. It was a very graphic scene."

Suspect arrested in deadly double stabbing

A man was detained at the scene and in an afternoon update, police identified the man as 32-year-old Elijah Hemingway. He has now been charged in Evans' death.

Police said Hemingway got into the house through an open window, went to the third floor and started stabbing the couple as they slept. They tried to fight back, police said.

Investigators said that Hemingway was found behind a nearby home with cuts to his hand and he was taken to a nearby hospital for treatment. KDKA's news crew at the scene witnessed Hemingway in handcuffs, being loaded into the back of an ambulance by first responders.

A motive is unknown.

"We do not know if there was any pre-existing relationship," Joseph said. "The woman did not know this male. We are trying to determine if the two males knew each other."

Hemingway is facing charges of criminal homicide, aggravated assault, burglary and trespassing. The alleged attack comes just a week before Hemingway was due back in court for a burglary in Pittsburgh earlier this year, court records show. He was released in that case on nonmonetary bond.

"Dr. Evans was a dedicated caregiver and valued member of our hospital and university communities," a UPMC spokesperson said in a statement. "Our thoughts are with his family, loved ones, and colleagues during this difficult time. We ask that their privacy be respected."

According to his profile with the University of Pittsburgh, Evans was the medical director of the Pediatric Critical Care Transport Team at UPMC Children's Hospital and an assistant professor of critical care medicine at the University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine.

Neighbor recounts deadly stabbing scene

Sandra Trappen lives in the home next door to where the stabbing took place and said she couldn't believe the number of police that were surrounding her house, only to find out that the suspect was hiding in her backyard.

"He was hiding, there's an area of my garden that's not particularly well manicured like the other parts," Trappen said. "He had found a way to conceal himself, but apparently he was injured and bleeding."

Trappen called the incident "incredibly shocking."

"Small and close-knit community"

Late Thursday morning, Edgewood police spoke out about what they called a tragic event in the community.

"We are a small and close-knit community and we are sure that many of you may be feeling shaken today," police said. "You may be sad, angry, anxious, distracted, or just having a hard time making sense of what happened."

Police asked that people be thoughtful about what they share in regard to the deadly incident, noting that things like rumors, graphic details, speculation and photographs can make an already difficult situation harder for those involved and others in the neighborhood.

World.title: Man wounded during 2024 Trump rally shooting in Butler County dies
World.content:
One of the men who was wounded in the attempted assassination of President Trump at a 2024 campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, has died.

In a statement on behalf of his family, Jim Copenhaver's lawyer confirmed the "devoted" husband, father and grandfather died on Wednesday, two years after he was "gravely wounded" during a shooting at a Trump rally. Coppenhaver died "from complications stemming from those wounds," Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday said.

In a statement, his family's lawyer said, "James's dedication to this great country was a defining part of his life. As a veteran, he proudly served our nation in the armed forces, and his love of country never wavered. James was a true American patriot who believed deeply in the freedoms and ideals upon which this nation was founded, and he embodied the very best traits of our great nation."

Mr. Trump offered his condolences to Copenhaver's family in a post on Truth Social, calling him "a true American Patriot."

"After being wounded while protecting his family, Jim showed tremendous bravery, courageously continuing to FIGHT, FIGHT, FIGHT, and maintaining a positive spirit despite unimaginable hardships. His indelible legacy of love and devotion will forever endure," Mr. Trump wrote.

House Republicans first announced the news on social media on Thursday.

"We are deeply saddened by the passing of Jim Copenhaver, who was gravely wounded in the horrific shooting in Butler, Pennsylvania," the tweet from the House GOP account read. "Jim endured unimaginable hardship with strength and perseverance. We join his family and loved ones in mourning his loss and praying for them during this difficult time."

Copenhaver was one of two rally-goers injured during the shooting on July 13, 2024. David Dutch of New Kensington was also injured and Corey Comperatore was killed.

One bullet hit Copenhaver in the triceps and another was lodged in his body after it took chunks of his colon, leaving him with nerve damage.

About a week after he was hospitalized, Copenhaver was discharged.

Both Copenhaver and Dutch spoke with KDKA-TV nearly a year after the assassination attempt and recalled the terror that broke out during the campaign rally for Mr. Trump.

"I was standing up looking at the Jumbotron behind me, and next thing I know my sleeve has been yanked," Copenhaver said. "I could see a portion of it going by pretty fast, and I heard 'pew.' I heard it, and I didn't realize at the time that I had gotten shot. But I turned around, and that's when I got the second shot."

Copenhaver was 76 years old.

World.title: Abraham Accords countries hold first official meeting since Oct. 7 attacks
World.content:
Ten blocks away from the United Nations General Assembly, U.S. diplomats quietly kickstarted the expansion of the Abraham Accords from the 43rd floor of a midtown Manhattan office tower.

On Thursday morning, State Department officials participated in the first official meeting of the Abraham Accords countries — the United States, Israel, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Morocco — since Oct. 7, 2023, when the Hamas attacks on Israel derailed the expansion of the Accords to more countries in the Middle East, Africa and Asia.

A meeting of nations who are part of the Abraham Accords in New York City on Sept. 24, 2026. N7 Foundation handout to CBS News

The Abraham Accords countries were joined Thursday for the first time by officials from Kazakhstan, which expressed an interest in joining the Accords last year.

The U.S. delegation was led by a senior State Department official, Under Secretary of Political Affairs Allison Hooker.

"Nearly three years after October 7, the Abraham Accords countries are back together," Hooker said, adding that President Trump brokered the historic agreements during his first term, and Thursday was an important signifier that the accords are "moving forward again."

The meeting was hosted by the N7 Foundation, a U.S.-based organization that has convened multilateral meetings of the Abraham Accords countries since 2021.

"The next phase is about deepening the relationships that already exist and identifying practical opportunities for countries to work together," said Jeffrey Talpins, founder of the N7 Foundation, who chaired the meeting.

Another senior administration official who was not authorized to speak publicly told CBS News that Secretary of State Marco Rubio's team and Steve Witkoff, the White House Special Envoy for Peace Missions, "are clearly prioritizing this effort."

Also present at the meeting were Aryeh Lightstone, special adviser to the Board of Peace, an international coalition dedicated to peace and reconstruction in Gaza, Ryan Arant, chief of staff to Under Secretary Hooker at the State Department, and Oren Eisner, president of the N7 Foundation.

The Abraham Accords are a set of agreements that normalized diplomatic relations between Israel and several Muslim countries. The first of a series of agreements was signed in 2020, toward the end of Mr. Trump's first term.

The UAE and Bahrain became the first two Gulf Arab countries to formally recognize Israel. Morocco soon followed.

Before the Oct. 7 Hamas attacks, momentum was building for Saudi Arabia and other Muslim countries to join the accords, but the attack and the wars in Gaza, Lebanon, and Iran that ensued stalled further expansion.

President Trump announced Kazakhstan's intention to join the Abraham Accords during an Oval Office meeting with Kazakhstan President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev in November 2025.

"We will soon announce a Signing Ceremony to make it official, and there are many more Countries trying to join this club of STRENGTH," Mr. Trump wrote on Truth Social at the time.

An official with the Kazakhstan embassy told CBS News that Thursday's gathering was a tangible step in the direction of expanding the accords.

"We are very excited about joining the Abraham Accords and all the partnership can do," he said. "We are interested in collaborations in technology and transport. Together we can do more than each individual country could do alone."

Participants discussed next steps to formalize cooperation among Abraham Accords countries, according to a person familiar with the meeting.

"The Abraham Accords have demonstrated what is possible when countries come together around shared interests with a common vision for a more integrated and prosperous region," Talpins said.

World.title: Trump to headline "Golden Age" event with top officials, tech executives
World.content:
President Trump is slated to speak on Tuesday in Washington at an event that he has billed as an "extraordinary gathering of America's greatest leaders, builders, innovators, and citizens," according to invitation materials obtained by CBS News.

The event will showcase the "people, ideas and innovations building America's Golden Age," according to the invitation materials, which said that Mr. Trump will deliver "an address to the nation."

The invitation touted special guests that include SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown and Palantir Chief Technology Officer Shyam Sankar, among others.

Several Trump administration officials are also named, including Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Secretary of Energy Chris Wright and NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. Karoline Leavitt, the former White House press secretary, is also named as a special guest.

"Together, we will celebrate the beginning of a new Golden Age — and reveal a bold vision for our nation's next 250 years," a note from Mr. Trump reads on the invitation materials. It adds that attendees will "be among the first to experience an unprecedented innovation from the White House — one that will forever change how your government recognizes you, respects your time, and serves you."

Mr. Trump's note added, "This will be more than an event. It will be a first look at America's future."

An agenda for the daylong event — which is set to take place several blocks from the White House at the Andrew W. Mellon Auditorium— listed a morning address by Mr. Trump and several panels on artificial intelligence, energy, space and other topics in the afternoon. It does not include a list of speakers.

The invitation materials for the event next week said that a dinner and afterparty are "sponsored exclusively" by a group called Horizon Events. It said the dinner and afterparty are "not official White House functions and are not paid for with government funds."

Mr. Trump is expected to meet on the same day as the event with House Speaker Mike Johnson and tech CEOs, according to two sources familiar with the matter who spoke on the condition of anonymity. Axios first reported on that planned meeting on Thursday.

The event comes as the Trump administration and tech industry leaders weigh whether to put guardrails on the development of advanced artificial intelligence.

In recent weeks, executives at frontier AI companies like Anthropic and OpenAI have called for limits on the speed of AI development in order to manage the risks posed by the technology. Others, including Nvidia's Huang, have argued that some warnings about AI dangers are overblown.

Mr. Trump has expressed skepticism, warning that limits on AI development by U.S. companies could cause China to take the lead. He signed an executive order earlier this year that allows companies to voluntarily submit powerful new AI models to the federal government for review before they are released to the public.

CBS News has reached out to the White House for comment.

World.title: California sheriff unlawfully seized ballots, state Supreme Court rules
World.content:
The California Supreme Court ruled Thursday that Riverside County Sheriff Chad Bianco violated the state's election law by ordering his deputies to seize more than 650,000 ballots tied to the Proposition 50 special election.

The justices ruled unanimously in two cases against Bianco, stating that he violated the law when he seized the ballots and also ignored directives from Attorney General Rob Bonta.

The court ordered Bianco to cease his investigation into election fraud claims and return the ballots to county officials. The court also said he must "refrain from further handling of the ballots except as necessary to comply with our order."

"In short, Bianco's arguments fail to persuade us that we should interpret section 15551 in a manner inconsistent with its plain text, which mandates that voted ballots remain in the custody of elections officials," the court wrote in its ruling.

In an  for his 2028 reelection campaign for Riverside County Sheriff, Bianco said the justices handed the Attorney General's Office "unchecked power over any investigation in the state of California."

"For that, the Court handed Bonta the power to pause a local criminal investigation and lock the evidence behind the Registrar," Bianco wrote. "I will obey the writs. I will not obey the message behind them — that local law enforcement works for Sacramento, not for the people who elected us."

Article V, Section 13 of the California Constitution, in part, states that the attorney general "shall be the chief law officer of the State" and sees that "the laws of the State are uniformly and adequately enforced."

It also states:

"The Attorney General shall have direct supervision over every district attorney and sheriff and over such other law enforcement officers as may be designated by law, in all matters pertaining to the duties of their respective offices, and may require any of said officers to make reports concerning the investigation, detection, prosecution, and punishment of crime in their respective jurisdictions as to the Attorney General may seem advisable."

The court also ruled unanimously that Bianco ignored directives from Bonta when he was told to pause his investigation.

"I'm grateful that our State Supreme Court reaffirmed my authority as Attorney General to supervise county sheriffs," Bonta wrote in a statement. "I take my responsibility to exercise that authority in the public interest seriously. This was an extraordinary situation that required extraordinary action."

In a video posted to social media, Bianco said the investigation "was never about the legality of the case," but rather whether "the attorney general had the ability to stop a lawful investigation into a crime."

He added that his office hoped that the California Supreme Court "would exercise basic common sense in their interpretation of our laws and our constitution."

"The framers of our constitution thought in terms of right versus wrong, good versus evil," Bianco said. "At that time, never would anyone have thought that we would have an attorney general who would prevent the investigation into criminal activity and corruption."

328.60 KB Cervantes v. Bianco The California Supreme Court ruled that Riverside County Sheriff Chad Bianco must cease his investigation into election fraud claims and return the seized ballots to county officials.

When the Riverside County Sheriff's Office seized the ballots earlier this year, Bianco, who lost his bid for California governor in the primaries, seized more than 611,000 ballots from the special election in which voters approved a redistricting measure that shifted five of California's Republican U.S. House seats to be more favorable to Democrats in the midterm elections this year.

Bianco claimed his agency was investigating a complaint from a local group alleging a possible discrepancy in which about 45,800 more votes were reported to California's Secretary of State. He described the probe as a "fact-finding mission."

The investigation faced fierce backlash, including legal challenges from California Attorney General Rob Bonta, UCLA's Voting Rights Project, whose lawsuit resulted in the court's decision, and local leaders in Riverside who petitioned to have the ballots returned to the Registrar's Office.

County elections officials also disputed Bianco's claim, saying the machine count and the final count submitted to the state differed by about 100 votes. The Riverside County Registrar of Voters said it "will continue to comply with all lawful court orders and with all legal obligations applicable to election materials and election administration."

After the filings, Bianco said in late March that he would pause his investigation "because of the politically motivated lawsuits and court filings" before the state Supreme Court ultimately issued a formal order to halt the probe in April.

The ballots were confiscated and held in an undisclosed location during the case, according to Riverside City Councilmember Clarissa Cervantes, one of the local leaders who petitioned the court.

Bianco echoed President Trump's allegations of election fraud in the 2020 election during a podcast appearance on the Ben Maynard Program in October 2025.

"We absolutely know there was fraud," Bianco alleged, claiming that "mail-in ballots are purposely designed for fraud."

He reiterated similar claims while the court heard oral arguments in August, claiming that the investigation was about "corruption in California."

"My message to Bonta is simple: you may have succeeded in burying the truth—for now," Bianco wrote following the decision. "But nothing stays hidden forever. In time, everything comes to light."

281.36 KB Bonta v. Bianco The California Supreme Court also ruled that Riverside County Sheriff Chad Bianco ignored directives from Attorney General Rob Bonta to pause his investigation into election fraud claims.

Democratic gubernatorial candidate and former state attorney general Xavier Becerra is part of UCLA's Voting Rights Project.

Over the weekend, Gov. Gavin Newsom signed a package of bills that would prevent anyone from seizing ballots.

"Today's ruling affirms that in California we will defend democracy — using every branch of government. And the new laws I signed just last week add new protections so attacks like this cannot happen again," Newsom wrote in response to the rulings. "People deserve to know their ballot is counted and secure, and in California we will do everything we can to protect that constitutional right — this year, and beyond."
