World.title: 23 Himveers battle weeks of gruelling Himalayan climbing to reach 24,131-ft Mt Abi Gamin & unfurl Tricolour
World.content:
23 ITBP Himveers have scaled Uttarakhandâs 7,355 metre Mt Abi Gamin.

A mountain near the frontier

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: 23 ITBP personnel conquered the 7,355-metre Mt Abi Gamin on the Indo-Tibet frontier in Uttarakhand, reaching its summit on September 16 and unfurling the Tricolour at an altitude of about 24,131 feet.Led by deputy commandant Parikshit Shah, the team began its expedition from ITBP headquarters in New Delhi on August 7. The climb took weeks of preparation, acclimatisation and movement through the difficult terrain of the Garhwal Himalayas.The expedition was part of the Force Level Mountaineering Expedition 2026 and was flagged off by ITBP director general Shatrujeet Kapur.At more than 7,000 metres, Abi Gamin presents a combination of thin air, freezing temperatures, snow and glacier terrain. Weather conditions can also change rapidly at such heights.The ITBP said the expedition demonstrated the force's mountaineering skills, determination and team spirit. After weeks on the mountain, the team finally reached the summit on September 16.The official ITBP account marked the achievement with the words, âHimveers summit Mt Abi Gamin!â, while highlighting the 23-member team's mountaineering skills, determination and team spirit.DG Shatrujeet Kapur also congratulated the expedition members.Mt Abi Gamin, also known as Ibi Gamin, is located in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district in the Garhwal Himalayas. It is close to Mt Kamet, with its summit located on the India-Tibet frontier and its northern slopes extending towards Tibet.The mountain is roughly 2 km northeast of Kamet and forms part of the wider Kamet massif.Abi Gamin has a long history of mountaineering. An Anglo-Swiss expedition made the first successful ascent in 1950 after approaching the mountain from the Tibetan side through Mana Pass. Indian mountaineers also successfully climbed it in the 1950s, including an expedition led by Nandu Jayal in 1953.Its location adds significance to the ITBP expedition, as the force has personnel operating regularly in high-altitude Himalayan areas.The challenge at more than 24,000 feet goes beyond the steepness of the mountain. Oxygen levels are much lower than at sea level, while extreme cold, snow, glaciers and sudden weather changes can make movement dangerous.The route around Abi Gamin has historically involved snow and glacier sections, with the mountain linked to nearby Kamet through Meade's Col. Earlier expeditions have reported difficult ice sections and extremely cold conditions at high camps.Such conditions make acclimatisation, careful planning and experience essential for any expedition to the summit.

World.title: Vote chori protest: Gaurav Gogoi, other Congress leaders detained; cops use water cannons in Patna, Chandigarh
World.content:
Water cannons used on Congress protesters in Chandigarh, Patna

Protests spread across states

CJP threatens nationwide protests

Youth Congress launches online petition

Rahul Gandhi steps up allegations

Priyanka backs Rahulâs allegations

ECI rejects claims of internal dissent

Chirag Paswan asks ECI to clarify

SC plea challenges Gyanesh Kumar

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Assam Congress chief Gaurav Gogoi and several party leaders were detained during a protest in Guwahati on Friday demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The detentions came as Congress workers staged demonstrations in several states over the functioning of the Election Commission.The Jantar mantar protest site has been closed for protestors whereas police used water cannons to disperse protesters in Chandigarh and Patna during the demonstrations.Security personnel were also deployed outside the Election Commission office in New Delhi ahead of a Delhi Congress demonstration over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The Indian Youth Congress was also scheduled to march from Raisina Road to Jantar Mantar.The protests follow an Indian Express report that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders related to the SIR process. The report said their concerns included voter registration, deletion and restoration of names and access to electoral-roll databases.The Madhya Pradesh Youth Congress held a protest outside the Chief Electoral Officerâs office in Bhopal on Thursday, demanding Kumarâs resignation. Protesters raised slogans against the CEC and carried posters reading âarrest Gyanesh Kumar for treasonâ and âVote-Chori magic trick exposedâ.In Dehradun, Congress workers also staged a protest demanding Kumarâs resignation, with Congress MP Kumari Selja leading the demonstration.In Punjab, Pradesh Congress Committee president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring demanded Kumarâs dismissal, an FIR against him and his alleged collaborators, and their arrest. He also announced a march to the ECI office in Chandigarh under the leadership of Sachin Pilot.In Karnataka, the Pradesh Congress Committee filed a police complaint seeking action against Kumar and BJP MLA Abhay Patil over alleged violations of voting rights and alleged attempts to manipulate electoral rolls. Congress alleged that Patil had sought deletion of eligible votersâ names and sought penal action against Kumar over alleged arbitrary deletions.Congress workers in Kolkata, West Bengal also staged a protest demanding the resignation of Kumar.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke on Friday said his organisation would launch nationwide protests from October 2 if Kumar did not resign by Saturday.In a post on X, Dipke said CJP would begin its protest from Mumbai on Gandhi Jayanti and subsequently take the agitation to cities across India.âIf Gyanesh Kumar does not resign by tomorrow, CJP will begin its nationwide protest from Mumbai on 2 October, and take it to cities across India. This Gandhi Jayanti letâs pledge to save democracy,â Dipke wrote.The announcement came a day after Dipke demanded Kumarâs resignation and threatened a âJantar Mantar 2.0â agitation if his demand was not met.The Indian Youth Congress on Thursday launched a nationwide online citizensâ petition titled âGyanesh, Itâs Done Broâ, seeking action against Kumar and urging citizens, particularly young people, to participate in a campaign for electoral transparency and accountability.The IYC has demanded Kumarâs removal as CEC, along with his arrest and prosecution. It has also sought a comprehensive investigation into electoral-roll processes, the alleged BJP connection raised by the campaign, and the release of electoral records and internal objections.Opposition plans removal motionOpposition parties are also preparing to move a motion seeking Kumarâs removal in both Houses of Parliament, with Congress reaching out to other opposition parties, party sources said. The notice is expected to be submitted in the coming days. A similar move is being prepared as the political dispute over the ECI and SIR continues.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Thursday alleged with â100 per cent certaintyâ that elections in India, including the 2024 Lok Sabha polls and several Assembly contests, had been âriggedâ. He demanded Kumarâs resignation and alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah were at the top of a conspiracy and would face investigation.âThe first thing we are saying is Mr. Gyanesh Kumar must resign immediately... This thing that you have done is an act against the Indian nation... A person who attacks the vote, who fundamentally destroys India's democratic institution, is nothing other than a 'Desh Drohi',â Gandhi said.He also said the CEC should âturn Approverâ.In Raipur, All India Adivasi Congress president Vikrant Bhuria defended Gandhiâs allegations of âvote theftâ, saying they were based on facts.âWhatever Rahul Gandhi says is based on facts, and history bears witness that every claim he has made has eventually been proven true. We had been campaigning for quite some time, under his leadership, against vote theft, highlighting that votes were being stolen, elections were being rigged, names were being deleted from voter lists, and the names of ineligible people were being added,â Bhuria told ANI.âInstances were found where thousands of voters were registered at a single address. He substantiated these claims with facts, yet the Election Commission failed to take cognizance of them,â he added.Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra defended Rahul Gandhiâs allegations and rejected the BJPâs response to the controversy.âI'm sorry, that's a very stale and weak story. There are facts, there is evidence. It is there for the whole country to see. My brother (Rahul Gandhi) has shown it in many different press conferences. He has put the evidence forward. Now it is very clear. 13 crore voters have been deleted. This is a lame excuse, and the BJP should stop making lame excuses. If they are meddling with our elections and if their leadership is making the Election Commission do this, then it is an act of treason and they should be aware of it. ..They are doing an illegal act. How many years has it been that they have been rigging elections? Naturally, they are so overconfident all the time...âAsked whether Congress was planning a protest, she said, âThere is a CWC meeting, I think, for which I am having to go back. So they will decide on that meeting and suppose what the course of action will be.âThe Election Commission has rejected the assertion that objections raised by Sandhu and Joshi represented structural or institutional dissent over final decisions. The poll panel has said operational queries, internal feedback and administrative suggestions raised during the drafting process are part of the normal functioning of a multi-member constitutional body. It has maintained that all final decisions, including those related to SIR, were unanimous.The ECI has also said ECINet is a secure, decentralised digital platform operated under the Representation of the People Acts, 1950 and 1951. According to the poll panel, statutory duties on the platform are carried out by designated field officers, including BLOs, AEROs, EROs, DEOs and CEOs, using unique IDs and secure credentials.Union minister Chirag Paswan said that if questions are being raised about the Election Commission, an independent constitutional body, the responsibility lies with the CEC to present his position clearly.âIf questions are being raised on Election Commission, which is an independent constitutional body, responsibility lies with CEC to present his stance clearly. It is problematic if people begin to doubt electoral process itself. EC needs to present its stance, not to Rahul Gandhi, but to public,â Paswan said.The controversy over the SIR exercise and the ECIâs internal functioning is expected to be taken up at the Congress Working Committee meeting scheduled for September 29 in New Delhi.A plea filed in the Supreme Court has challenged alleged unilateral decisions taken by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in connection with the Election Commissionâs electoral-roll revision exercise, including the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).The petitioner has sought an SIT investigation into the alleged deletion of around 13 crore voters from electoral rolls. The plea also seeks a declaration that decisions allegedly taken without the concurrence of the other two Election Commissioners were illegal.It has further sought restoration of the original Form 6 used for voter registration and prosecution of Gyanesh Kumar, Deputy Election Commissioner Maneesh Garg and ECI IT head Seema Khanna for alleged violations of their duties under the Representation of the People Act.

World.title: 'Must maintain the trust of people': Chirag Paswan urges EC to 'firmly present its side' amid SIR row
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union minister Chirag Paswan on Friday urged the Election Commissioner to "firmly present its side" amid the ongoing row over the internal disagreements in the poll panel.

Speaking to reporters, Chirag said the Election Commission must retain people's trust and address their doubts about the electoral process.

"If such questions are being raised against the Election Commission, I believe it is also the responsibility of the Election Commission, especially the CEC, to firmly present its side," the Union minister said.

"I don't care what the opposition says because it is their job is to do politics.

The Election Commission must maintain the trust of the people because if doubts arise in the public's mind about the electoral process itself, that would be wrong. In such a situation, the Election Commission should firmly put forth its points so that no doubts arise in the people's minds," he added.

This comes after the opposition demanded Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation after an Indian Express report highlighted differences among members of the EC over the SIR of electoral rolls.





The report said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi raised formal objections on at least 14 occasions over a 10-month period against decisions and orders related to electoral-roll processes.

Earlier on Thursday, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi accused the CEC of "vote chori, kanun chori, sanstha chori (vote theft, law theft, institutional theft)", calling it an "act against the nation".

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"The Election Commission is the institutional protector of the vote... I have shown it with proof, and there is already more than enough information to make this a 100% certainty that Indian elections, Lok Sabha elections, 2024 election, Vidhan Sabha elections are all being rigged," he said, addressing a press conference.

The Election Commission, however, described the queries and observations raised by its members as part of its routine internal process. It said written notes, technical inputs and internal scrutiny were standard mechanisms to check legal compliance and protect voters' rights.

The ECI further said all decisions taken by the Commission, including those related to SIR, had full legal backing and stressed that its final decisions were unanimous.

World.title: Ganesh immersion 2026 LIVE: Khairatabad Ganesh idol immersion passes off without hitch; traffic curbs across central Hyderabad till September 26
World.content:
The immersion of Khairatabad Ganesh idol in the Hussain Sagar lake, Hyderabad, passed off without a hitch on Friday (September 25, 2026) afternoon at about 2.25 p.m.

The delay by over two hours for the key marker in the immersion schedule upset the rest of the day’s line-up as the main path between Telephone Bhavan, Secretariat road and Necklace Road was out of bounds for the other idols streaming towards the lake from as far off places as Balapur.

Meanwhile, the famous 21–kg Balapur Ganesh laddu fetched a record ₹39 lakh at the annual auction with Sama Praneeth Reddy, founder of Urban Group Private Limited, placing the winning bid. The idols procession too was en route to Tank Bund. Arrangements were made for the immersion of the idols from other parts of the city.

Also read: Immersion procession of Khairatabad Ganesh idol in Hyderabad gets delayed start

For commuters, that means a large part of central Hyderabad will effectively belong to the procession for much of Friday (September 25, 2026) and into Saturday (September 26, 2026) morning.

Also read: File compliance report over loud music during Ganesh idol procession, immersion: HC to police

No traffic other than vehicles carrying Ganesh idols will be permitted along the main procession route from 6 a.m. on Friday (September 25, 2026) until 10 a.m. on Saturday (September 26, 2026). Restrictions on NTR Marg, PVNR Marg, Tank Bund and Khairatabad Flyover could continue until Saturday evening, depending on the progress of immersion.

Follow the LIVE for more updates

World.title: Election Commission row LIVE: Protests mount against CEC Gyanesh Kumar amid dissent allegations
World.content:
Opposition parties are demanding Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, with CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke alleging the elections are “rigged” and the Congress planning a protest at Jantar Mantar.

The row follows an Indian Express report stating that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over 10 months, alleging that key decisions were taken in the name of the full Commission without their knowledge, some of them “unauthorised and illegal.”

Also read: Opposition calls for CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s removal after report on Election Commissioners’ dissent

The Election Commission said “differing views” are part of its decision-making process, as the poll panel carries out a nationwide revision of the electoral database.

The BJP hit back, with MP Sudhanshu Trivedi calling Mr. Gandhi a “master of deception” and citing the Congress’s prolonged absence from power in Tamil Nadu and West Bengal.

Also watch: LoP Rahul Gandhi addresses Delhi press briefing amid ECI dissent row over SIR

World.title: In pictures: Ganesh's journey through Mumbai
World.content:
Maharashtra’s elaborate Ganesh Chaturthi pandals transform the state into a celebration of culture and faith every year. Mumbai especially creates large pandals in every neighbourhood and celebrates the festival for 10 days. Thousands of people visit these creations during this period and with every year, the fervour and crowds have only increased. After the festival, the grand stage / shrine is dismantled and the clay idols are immersed at sea.

Ganesh Chaturthi festival in Mumbai has been defining its cultural identity for the last several years. From start to finish, the city celebrates the occasion with pride. An artist gives final touches to a Ganesh idol inside a workshop at Parel in Mumbai.

Mumbai organises large pandals in many areas. A ganesh idol ‘Fort cha Yuvraj’ is taken via BMC headquarters and CSMT building towards the pandal before the festival in Mumbai.

Mumbai's Parel area also comes alive with devotion during this period. Firecrackers lighting up the streets during the procession of 'Parel cha Raja' as the idol reaches its pandal.

Many people get involved in making the festival a grand success. People throng around the Chandanwadi area’s 'Goad Ganpati' during its aagman in Girgaon.

Mumbai's Lalbaug area creates an elaborately themed pandal every year. The entry gate outside Lalbaugcha Raja pandal being set up before the celebrations. Thousands of people including celebrities visit these pandals.

Lalbaugcha Raja is Mumbai's most famous idol as it was established in 1934. This pandal witnesses an overwhelming footfall every year. A massive crowd of devotees offer prayers and seek the blessings of Lord Ganesha. The primary reason for its immense popularity is the deep belief that this Ganesha is a Navasacha Ganapati, meaning 'the one who fulfils all wishes'. Devotees truly believe that praying here with sincere devotion ensures their desires are granted. Several celebrities and public figures have been seen seeking blessings from Lord Ganesha at Mumbai’s famous Lalbaugcha Raja pandal since the festival started.

This year, September 25, 2026 was the last day of these festivities where idols are taken to the sea to be immersed. 'Tejukaya cha Raja' on its way towards Girgaon Chowpatty beach for immersion on the last day of Ganeshotsav festival in Mumbai on September 25, 2026.

'Tejukaya cha Raja' was given a grand send-off as the idol emerged out from the pandal, as the Ganeshotsav comes to an end. At Swarajyabhoomi (Girgaon Chowpatty), one of the major immersion locations, the civic body has arranged 12 artificial ponds, 20 observation towers, 22 rafts, 90 toilets, three ambulances and around 1,000 personnel.

Devotees bid farewell to 'Mumbaicha Raja' amid celebrations, as the idol is being taken to the sea on Friday, September 25, 2026. The BMC said that it has made necessary arrangements at 67 natural immersion sites, including 44 beaches and jetties and 23 natural lakes, for idols more than six feet in height.

'Parel cha Maharaja' being taken to the sea by devotees for the 'visarjan'. Girgaon Chowpatty is one of Mumbai's key immersion points. The civic body has deployed 25,000 personnel for looking after immersion arrangements in the city.

Devotees participate in a procession as 'Parel cha Lambodar' was being taken to the Girgaon Chowpatty beach in Mumbai. Several processions were accompanied by traditional dhol-tasha troupes, while devotees danced and chanted devotional slogans.

World.title: Supreme Court rejects PIL for setting up panel to examine use of Hindi as official language of apex court
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Friday (September 25, 2026) refused to entertain a PIL seeking directions to the Centre to constitute a commission to examine and recommend the use of Hindi as an official language of the apex court.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said language-related reforms were already being considered administratively and could not be brought about through judicial orders.

The PIL, filed by Brahmeshwar Nath Mishra, sought a direction to the Centre to constitute a commission for making recommendations regarding the use of Hindi as the official language of the Supreme Court.

Appearing for Mr. Mishra, an advocate submitted that the Centre could be directed to constitute such a commission and referred to various constitutional provisions in support of the plea.

The CJI said the Supreme Court was already introducing language-related reforms in a gradual and phased manner.

“We are now giving a brief description of all the reports in Hindi. We will start with other regional languages,” the CJI said, adding the court would maintain the country's linguistic culture and respect regional languages.

The CJI further said such reforms could not be implemented through judicial orders.

“These things do not happen through court orders. They happen as part of reforms, slowly and in a phased manner. Such things we are doing,” the CJI said.

The Bench also pointed out that the relief sought in the PIL would entail a constitutional amendment.

The counsel, however, pressed for at least a direction to constitute a commission,

However, the Bench dismissed the PIL.

World.title: Adani Group debuts at Kolkata’s Durga Puja celebrations
World.content:
The Adani Group, which is exploring an investment roadmap in West Bengal, has decided to make its debut at the largest cultural and religious festival of the State — Durga Puja.

Gautam Adani, chairman of the Adani Group during his visit to Kolkata on September 24 had announced that his group will build a curated Durga Puja programme to celebrate Bengal’s artistes and take Maa to audiences across the world.

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said that Memorandum of Understandings (MoUs) with Adani Enterprises were signed to explore “cultural initiatives connected with Durga Puja and Bengal’s wider artistic heritage traditions.

“Two meaningful MoUs were signed today. One is about heritage preservation and restoration of the Writers’ Buildings, and the second is about Durga Puja. It’s the main festival of West Bengal,” Mr. Adhikari said.

Adani Group has launched its official website for Durga Puja Adani Preview (DPAP) 2026.

All Durga Pujas across Kolkata, Bidhannagar, and the South Dum Dum municipality area have been invited to register through the official website by 25 September 2026. Each of the eight selected pujas will receive a grant of ₹25 lakh from Adani Group, which includes ₹10 lakh will be awarded to the artist and ₹15 lakh will be awarded to the Puja Committee.

“The maiden Adani Preview will comprise eight pujas across Kolkata — a number we hope will grow in the years to come,” the website of DPAP said.

The preview dates for the DDPAP are 10–12 October, from 6 p.m. to 4 a.m.

According to the DPAP, the preview will facilitate a convenient and hassle-free puja viewing experience for thousands who seek to avoid the late-Puja viewing rush. “This affirms the commitment of Adani Group to the welfare of Bengal,” the website states.

Before Durga Puja Adani Preview, massArt, a non profit organisation used to organise a preview of Durga Puja from 2022. This year massArt will showcase 24 contemporary Durga Puja Art.

World.title: Greens take on Church, political leaderships over ‘threats’ to Idukki Collector for enforcing court orders on environmental protection
World.content:
Ten environmental organisations in Keralam have demanded an end to the alleged smear campaign and threats against the Idukki District Collector for implementing Supreme Court and High Court orders.

In a statement, the organisations pointed out that the Collector was “only carrying out” the Supreme Court order for the removal of illegal fences, walls and other obstructions erected on government revenue land illegally occupied by forest encroachers, land mafias and certain religious organisations, particularly those blocking elephant corridors; and the Kerala High Court’s directive to remove illegal constructions in five panchayats.

The statement said the State government should initiate contempt of court proceedings against those, including “MLAs, an MP, the Idukki Diocese and the Marxist party”, who have allegedly issued threats against Collector Dinesan Cheruvatt, who is also the chairperson of the Idukki District Disaster Management Authority.

He should be extended adequate protection, they stated in emails sent to the Chief Minister, the Forest Minister, the Revenue Minister, the Chief Secretary, and the secretaries of the Revenue and Forest departments.

The order issued on September 23, 2026 by Mr. Cheruvatt is “historic” and will determine the future of environmental sustainability and the rule of law in Keralam, they said.

When the legality of commercial establishments, resorts and other illegal structures built across wildlife corridors is questioned, those responsible attempt to portray the issue as one affecting ordinary believers and farmers. A political-Church alliance is mobilising the public to protect vested interests, the organisations alleged.

The State government should not tolerate the practice of personally targeting government officials to protect vote banks or creating fear and communal divisions to intimidate public institutions into submission. No diocese or Church authority could claim to be above the law. Idukki is “not an independent nation”, they remarked.

Traditional elephant corridors have been blocked by large resorts, tourism infrastructure and concrete walls, forcing elephants into farms and human settlements. The reluctance of Church leaders and politicians to acknowledge the basic reality that elephants will continue to enter inhabited areas unless such obstructions are removed stems from an attempt to protect commercial interests, they said.

They also called for greater transparency regarding the ongoing joint inspections by the Revenue, Forest and Local Self-Government departments, and urged the authorities to keep the public informed about their findings.

The organisations also appealed to Church leaders and politicians to “refrain from unnecessarily intervening” in environmental matters and misleading the public. They called for the scientific restoration of elephant corridors and the installation of AI-based surveillance systems and hanging fences in vulnerable areas to ensure the safety of farmers.

World.title: Alleged Myanmar-based extremists kill four Nagas in Manipur
World.content:
GUWAHATI

Alleged Myanmar-based extremists killed four Nagas in Manipur’s Kamjong district on Thursday afternoon (September 24, 2026).

The Working Committee of the Tangkhul Naga Long (WC-TNL), the top body of the Tangkhul community, condemned the cross-border attack at Pilong village near India’s border with Myanmar.

In a statement on Friday (September 25, 2026), the WC-TNL said members of the Kuki National Army-Burma and Kuki elements backed by Myanmar-based People’s Defence Force carried out the attack.

“A Kuki terror group armed heavily with sophisticated weapons crossed the river Namya from Phailen Kuki village of Myanmar and launched a violent attack on Pilong civilians,” the WC-TNL said, holding the Indian government responsible for the cross-border terrorism and killings.

It said two residents were shot dead in the vicinity of the village, while the two others were taken away to adjoining Phailen and killed by the assailants.

The WC-TNL identified the deceased as Betterson Jajo of Kangpat Khunou; Vareishim Jajo and Phami Jajo, a father-son duo hailing from Kangpat Khullen village; and Ningthem Kashak, a resident of Zingsui village.

“Five residents were keeping watch at Pilong settlement area when the violent incident took place. Of the five, one managed to escape from the village and was rescued by a team of Tangkhul civil society organisations at around 9.45 p.m.,” the organisation said.

The survivor was identified as Akhan Kaping, a native of Hunphun village in Ukhrul district.

The WC-TNL said this was the third such attack on Naga villagers along the India-Myanmar border in Kamjong district. It lamented that despite the repeated attacks, the State government as well as the border guards, including Assam Rifles, remained “lackadaisical” and failed to protect the vulnerable villagers living along the border.

World.title: Kerala LoP Pinarayi Vijayan seeks removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, halt to SIR
World.content:
Leader of Opposition in the Keralam Assembly Pinarayi Vijayan on Friday (September 25, 2026) sought the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar and demanded that the SIR of electoral rolls be halted.

In a post on ‘X’, the senior CPI (M) leader said “revelations” about objections raised by two Election Commissioners over decisions concerning voter registration, deletion of names and Special Intensive Revision (SIR) raised “grave questions” about the functioning of the Election Commission of India.

The revelations about objections raised by two Election Commissioners over decisions concerning voter registration, deletion of names and #SIR raise grave questions about the functioning of the ECI. CEC Gyanesh Kumar must be removed, SIR must be halted, the voting rights of those… — Pinarayi Vijayan (@pinarayivijayan) September 25, 2026

His remarks came amid a newspaper report of differences within the three-member EC over several decisions and instructions relating to electoral-roll revision, including deletion and addition of names, changes in forms for new voters, and access to voter data.

“Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar must be removed, SIR must be halted, the voting rights of those wrongfully excluded must be restored, and the independence and credibility of the EC must be protected,” the former Chief Minister said.

He said the right to vote belongs to the people of India. “It cannot be manipulated to serve the political interests of the BJP and Sangh Parivar,” Mr. Vijayan charged.

World.title: Dar, Saudi and Turkish counterparts review progress on institutionalising tripartite defence pact
World.content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar met his Saudi Arabian and Turkish counterparts on Friday to review progress on institutionalising the tripartite Makkah Defence Alliance.

The agreement — signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on August 7 — empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all. Its inaugural meeting was held on Aug 31, where officials from all member states met in Istanbul to establish the institutional structure of the alliance, and Pakistan was picked to head its secretariat in Riyadh.

Retired Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood was appointed as the first secretary general on September 23.

Dar met Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan and Turkiye’s Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan at the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, he said in a post on social media platform X.

“Under the framework of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA), we reviewed progress towards establishing the institutional structures under the agreement and exchanged views on regional and international security issues,” he wrote.

‘Urgent’ meeting of chiefs of staff to be held

Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Ministry, in a post on X, said the meeting was held within the framework of the agreement, where the three member states condemned the recent Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia and discussed arrangements to convene an “urgent meeting of the chiefs of staff of the three countries” to support the Gulf state within the pact.

“They commended the vigilance of the Saudi armed forces and their ability to defend the kingdom’s security,” the statement said, adding that Saudi Arabia held the right to take measures “it deems appropriate” in self-defence.

It added that the three sides reviewed progress on the establishment of the general secretariat, committees, and working groups, as well as “preparations for the commencement of their activities”.

The three also exchanged views on the prevailing situation in the region and underscored the “importance of upholding the principles of international law, good neighbourliness, mutual respect for state sovereignty, non-interference in internal affairs, and ensuring the security and freedom of maritime navigation”.

The three sides reiterated their determination to work towards peace and stability in the region and push for peaceful solutions to existing crises, the Saudi Foreign Ministry said.

Later, Turkiye’s Defence Ministry said its Chief of General Staff General Selcuk Bayraktaroglu will travel to Saudi Arabia to meet his Saudi and Pakistani counterparts as part of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement.

A day earlier, Saudi Arabia intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by Yemen’s Houthis after issuing warnings for several regions, including the holy city of Makkah.

As Yemen’s Houthi rebels continue to attack Saudi Arabia, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry on Sept 18 said that Pakistan would go to “any extent” to defend Saudi Arabia, adding that Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s security was “unconditional”.

On Wednesday, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had also vowed to stand “shoulder to shoulder” with Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its sovereignty and security.

Additional input from Reuters.

World.title: Delegate walkout, protests greet Netanyahu as he addresses UN General Assembly
World.content:
NEW YORK: Dozens of delegates walked out of the UN General Assembly hall on Thursday as hundreds of protesters gathered outside the building while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu defended Tel Aviv’s actions amid growing international isolation, with elections looming that could threaten his political future.

The walkout undersco­red the competing pressu­res facing Netanyahu, who is battling mounting criticism abroad over the Gaza conflict while campaigning for re-election at home ahead of an October 27 vote.

On Thursday, Netanyahu delivered a combative address inside the General Assembly, where dozens of delegations walked out as he began speaking.

The departing diplomats left large sections of the hall empty, creating a striking contrast with Netanyahu’s attempt to use the podium to present Israel’s case before the international community.

Netanyahu responded by accusing his critics of hypocrisy and calling them “moral cowards.”

He rejected allegations that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza, saying Israel had prevented rather than committed genocide. He defended the country’s military actions in Gaza and elsewhere in the region.

Delegates walk out of the General Assembly hall as Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu arrives to address the 81st United Nations General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York City, US, September 24. — Reuters

He also devoted a significant part of his speech to New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, calling him “the antisemitic mayor of New York” and accusing him of spreading what Netanyahu described as lies about Israel.

Mamdani, who had declined to join the street protests, responded after the speech.

“Prime Minister Netanyahu used his speech to repeat baseless lies meant to sanitise his genocide of Palestinians,” Mamdani said.

“No lie can change the fact that he remains the subject of an International Criminal Court arrest warrant alleging war crimes and crimes against humanity.”

Mamdani previously said New York City lacked the authority to enforce the ICC warrant against Netanyahu, arguing that the appropriate authorities should carry it out.

On Wednesday night, the mayor had hosted Palestinian families from Gaza at Gracie Mansion and planted an olive tree with them, saying: “May peace be our future.”

The two scenes — protesters confronting his government’s policies on the streets and diplomats leaving the hall during his address — turned Netanyahu’s brief visit to New York into a day of parallel confrontation.

Netanyahu’s stay had already been sharply shortened amid security concerns and expectations of protests. He arrived on Thursday morning, addressed the General Assembly and was scheduled to return to Israel the same evening rather than remain in New York overnight.

Outside the UN, Jewish and Muslim activists, Palestinian supporters, human-rights campaigners, progressive Jewish groups, politicians, artists and musicians took part in separate demonstrations across Manhattan. Their messages varied, but opposition to Netanyahu’s government and Israel’s conduct of the Gaza war brought many of them into the streets at the same time.

Demonstrators protest after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s address to the United Nations 81st General Assembly in New York City, U.S., September 24. — Reuters

The protests also offered a visible glimpse of a generational shift in American attitudes toward Israel and Netanyahu. While support for Israel remains stronger among older Americans, younger Americans have become substantially more critical of the Israeli government.

A Pew Research Centre survey conducted in May found that only 18 per cent of Americans aged 18 to 29 had a favourable view of the Israeli government, compared with 47pc among those aged 65 and older. Among the youngest Americans, 58pc expressed a favourable view of Palestinians, compared with 47pc among those 65 and older.

That generational divide was visible on the streets of New York, where many of the demonstrators were young people, including students, activists, artists and younger politicians.

The largest direct action outside the UN was organised by Jewish Voice for Peace, whose New York chapter brought hundreds of protesters to First Avenue and 39th Street. Demonstrators wearing matching white T-shirts sat in the roadway, chanting against Netanyahu and calling for an end to US support for Israel.

For a while, protesters stood and sat in the street, linking arms and blocking traffic as police moved in to clear the roadway. The chants continued as officers began making arrests.

At least 30 people, including actors and politicians, were arrested in the initial action. Police later said more than 100 protesters had been taken into custody.

Among those detained were actors Susan Sarandon and Hannah Einbinder, congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier and City Council member Chi Ossé. Musicians Julien Baker and Lucy Dacus and actor Elliott Page were also among the prominent figures taking part in the protests.

Chelsea Manning, who joined the protest, said people outside government institutions needed ways to reject policies they regarded as imperialism, ethnic cleansing and genocide.

“We can’t be in there. This is the closest that we can get,” she said.

Manijeh Moradian, a university professor of Iranian and Jewish heritage who participated in the demonstration, said protesters had a responsibility to speak out against what was happening in Gaza with US support.

Jewish groups divided

The demonstrations also highlighted divisions within New York’s Jewish community.

Progressive Jewish organisations, including New York Jewish Agenda, T’ruah, J Street, New Jewish Narrative, New Israel Fund and Partners for Progressive Israel, held a separate protest at Dag Hammarskjöld Plaza near the UN.

“We are gathered here as American Jews, Israelis, New Yorkers, to say: You are not welcome here,” said Margo Hughes-Robinson, executive director of New York Jewish Agenda.

T’ruah, a rabbinic human-rights organisation, called for a ceasefire and accountability for alleged war crimes. The organisers described their rally as an alternative for Jewish New Yorkers who opposed Netanyahu’s policies while retaining concern for Israel and Jewish security.

They were confronted by pro-Netanyahu counter-protesters who blew whistles, used megaphones, chanted “Bibi”, and sang Israel’s national anthem.

On the other side, the ultra-Orthodox anti-Zionist group Neturei Karta also demonstrated, arguing that opposition to Israel could not automatically be equated with antisemitism.

Elsewhere, Jewish and Muslim demonstrators marched together towards the UN, while Palestinian activists and other organisations joined the broader mobilisation against Netanyahu.

A city divided over Israel and Gaza

As police loaded detained protesters onto buses outside the UN, Netanyahu was speaking inside a building protected by heavy security. Outside, demonstrators sought to challenge the Israeli prime minister’s account of the Gaza war; inside, diplomats expressed their opposition by leaving the chamber.

The contrast was difficult to miss.

For several hours on Thursday, New York’s streets and the UN General Assembly hall became parallel stages for the same international argument — one expressed through demonstrations and arrests outside, the other through a diplomatic boycott inside.

And beneath both scenes was a changing American debate over Israel.

World.title: LHC seeks Punjab home secretary's reply on plea against Aleema's detention
World.content:
LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Friday sought a reply from the Punjab home secretary on a petition challenging the detention of PTI founder Imran Khan’s sister, Aleema Khan, under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance.

Aleema was detained by authorities on Sept 20, after the office of Lahore’s deputy commissioner (DC) ordered her detention or arrest for 30 days. The DC’s order cited a letter by the Lahore capital city police officer, which referred to police reports that Aleema and Ameer “are prejudicial to the public safety and maintenance of public order”.

Justice Abher Gul Khan has been holding hearings on the petition. In the previous hearing, Justice Abher had sought arguments on the plea’s maintainability.

As the hearing resumed on Friday, a Punjab government law officer asked the court to dispose of the petition, arguing that the home secretary had already fixed a hearing to review the detention order issued by the Lahore DC on Sept 28.

The judge, however, issued a notice to the home secretary for submission of a reply to the petition.

Barrister Taimur Malik submitted that his client, Aleema, was facing difficulties in receiving her medicines and other essentials in jail. The judge directed the counsel to file a separate application on this issue.

Aleema’s detention took place amid reports of a crackdown on the PTI ahead of its September 27 countrywide protest and march to Islamabad, which the party has called to demand Imran’s release from jail and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution.

Shahraiz Khan, Aleema’s son, filed a petition through Advocate Rana Mudassar Umar, challenging the detention orders issued by the Lahore DC against his mother and two aunts.

Following Aleema’s detention, her two sisters, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, were also detained under MPO. A day earlier, the LHC turned down a request to immediately suspend the preventive detention notifications issued against Noreen and Dr Uzma.

The petition contends that the DC unlawfully issued the detention orders and failed to follow the procedure prescribed under Section 3 of the MPO Ordinance.

It further argues that the orders contain no specific allegations and demonstrate no application of mind.

The petition also says that ordinary criminal law and less restrictive measures were not considered and contends that the grounds for detention were not communicated within the required period, alleging that the detention orders were issued after the arrests.

It asks the court to set aside the detention orders issued by the Lahore DC and declare them unlawful.

World.title: Pakistan's economy stable, moving towards growth, PM Shehbaz tells business delegation
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday said Pakistan’s economy had stabilised and was moving towards growth, while inviting US-based Pakistani business leaders to explore investment opportunities in the country.

Speaking at a meeting with delegations from the US-Pakistan Business Council and US Business Council for International Understanding (BCIU) on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, the prime minister said Pakistan had undertaken “massive structural reforms”, including the digitisation of the economy, the Federal Board of Revenue and e-governance.

“Our economy is now stable. We have moved towards growth,” he said, adding that the Gulf crisis had affected Pakistan at an unfavourable time.

“We are trying to stand on our feet. We are doing our best to facilitate peace efforts,” he said.

The premier said Pakistan had been “largely very successful” in June, but the situation had subsequently deteriorated. He expressed hope that, with the support of friendly and brotherly countries, the situation could be brought under control and long-term peace achieved in the region.

He said regional peace was important for discussions on business and investment.

The prime minister identified agriculture, mining, information technology and artificial intelligence-led initiatives, energy security, and investment, imports and shipments as key areas of potential cooperation.

On agriculture, he said Pakistan could benefit from modern machinery and technology, including combine harvesters and other equipment, to improve efficiency, increase production and reduce costs.

“Pakistan has the biggest potential” in agriculture, he said.

The prime minister also highlighted the country’s mineral resources, saying Pakistan had been “blessed” with enormous potential in the mining sector.

He said IT and AI-led initiatives also offered significant potential, particularly given Pakistan’s young population. The government was seeking to empower young people through vocational and skills training, he added.

“This is a great asset for Pakistan,” he said, adding that the workforce could be utilised through productive employment and increased production.

The prime minister also pointed to lessons from the ongoing regional crisis, saying Pakistan offered security and safety for energy reserves, including petrol, oil and gas.

He also highlighted investment, imports and shipments as areas for discussion with the business delegation.

PM Shehbaz said privatisation was another important area of interest for investors.

Shehbaz further said Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) was being privatised and expressed confidence that its new Pakistani owners would turn the airline around.

The government had also privatised a bank, while power distribution companies in various provinces were being processed for privatisation, he said.

“Many other areas of mutual interest are being offered to the private sector,” the prime minister said.

“The government’s business is to facilitate, act as a catalyst to support the private sector, not become the private sector,” he added.

PM Shehbaz, UN chief discuss Middle East peace

Prime Minister Shehbaz also met UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres, with the two discussing major regional and international developments, including the situation in the Middle East, the government said in a post on X.

According to the post, the prime minister stressed the importance of dialogue and diplomacy in resolving regional tensions and reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to promoting peace and stability in the region.

He reaffirmed Pakistan’s “steadfast commitment to multilateralism and the central role of the UN in promoting international peace and development”.

The two leaders also discussed the situation in Afghanistan and the “drastic increase” in terrorism emanating from Afghan soil.

The prime minister reiterated Pakistan’s strong attachment to the purposes and principles of the UN Charter and appreciated Guterres’s leadership in upholding them.

He also reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for the Palestinian people’s right to self-determination and statehood.

The prime minister raised concerns over the “rising trend of Islamophobia”, particularly in Pakistan’s immediate neighbourhood, and called for effective international action to curb it.

Guterres, meanwhile, commended Pakistan’s role and strong voice at the UN, as well as its contribution to international peace and security.

He appreciated Pakistan’s mediation efforts for the peaceful resolution of conflicts and durable peace and stability in the region.

The UN secretary general also appreciated Pakistan’s role and sacrifices in countering terrorism.

In a separate post on X, the UN said Guterres had “expressed appreciation for Pakistan’s important role as an elected member of the Security Council” and its support for the UN.

PM meets Prince Rahim

PM Shehbaz also met Prince Rahim al-Hussaini Aga Khan V in New York, where he lauded the “long-standing” contributions of the Ismaili community to Pakistan’s socio-economic development.

The premier “reiterated his resolve to continue close cooperation with him to achieve shared goals of peace, stability, and development”, according to a post on the government’s X account.

PM Shehbaz also lauded the Aga Khan Development Network (AKDN) for its work in financial inclusion, tourism promotion, cultural heritage preservation, and fostering economic empowerment. He also stressed the need to leverage potential for further cooperation in the sectors.

Prince Rahim, for his part, appreciated Pakistan’s efforts for regional peace and stability and reaffirmed commitment to strengthening partnership with Pakistan.

“He also expressed a desire to continue and expand cooperation in various sectors of human development — particularly health, education, resilience to the impacts of climate change, and sustainable socio-economic development — for the welfare of the people of Pakistan,” the statement read.

PM Shehbaz further invited Prince Rahim to visit Pakistan “to further strengthen and deepen the bonds of friendship and cooperation established over several decades”.

Dar meets Bahrain, Singapore foreign ministers

Meanwhile, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar met Bahrain’s Foreign Minister Dr Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, the Foreign Office (FO) said.

“The two sides discussed bilateral relations, including preparations for the forthcoming third session of the Joint Ministerial Commission”, the FO said in a post on X.

They also exchanged views on regional and international developments.

Al Zayani appreciated Pakistan’s constructive role in promoting regional peace and stability, it added.

The two foreign ministers reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening bilateral cooperation and maintaining close coordination at bilateral and multilateral forums.

Dar also met his Singaporean counterpart Vivian Balakrishnan on the sidelines of the UNGA, FO said in a separate post.

“The two sides reviewed bilateral relations and exchanged views on further strengthening cooperation in diverse areas of mutual interest”, the FO said.

They agreed that “sustained engagement and high-level exchanges” would help deepen bilateral ties and advance mutually beneficial cooperation, it added.

The two foreign ministers also discussed regional and international developments of mutual interest.

Balakrishnan appreciated Pakistan’s efforts to promote dialogue and diplomacy in addressing regional challenges, the statement added.

World.title: Pakistan secure another Asian Games medal as Noor, Ashab reach squash semis
World.content:
Pakistan secured another medal at the Asian Games on Friday after Noor Zaman and Mohammad Ashab Irfan won their respective singles matches to reach the semi-finals of the squash competition.

Third-seeded Noor defeated Hong Kong’s Chi Hin Henry Leung, while fifth-seeded Ashab overcame India’s Veer Chotrani at the Nagoya Kinjo Futo Arena to put Pakistan into the medal rounds of the event.

Noor, Pakistan’s top-ranked player in the draw, was pushed by Leung but held his nerve to secure a place in the last four. Ashab also produced a strong performance against the fourth-seeded Indian, recovering from losing the opening game to win 3-1.

Ashab prevailed 6-11, 11-8, 11-6, 11-6 to avenge Pakistan’s defeat to India in the men’s team final at the previous Asian Games.

The victories mean Pakistan are assured of at least a bronze medal in the men’s singles competition, with the losing semi-finalists awarded bronze.

The two Pakistanis had reached the quarter-finals without dropping a game, with Noor defeating Kuwait’s Ammar Altamimi 11-4, 11-9, 11-4 and Ashab overcoming Saudi Arabia’s Mohammad Al Alnafsan 11-9, 11-3, 11-5 in the last 16 on Thursday.

Noor and Ashab will now contest their respective semi-finals on Saturday, with a place in Sunday’s final at stake.

World.title: Trump to wrap up Xi summit with a tour of US archives
World.content:
US President Donald Trump will follow up his summit with Xi Jinping by taking the Chinese leader on Friday to the US National Archives, where they are expected to stress views about the history and direction of ties between their countries.

Thursday’s lavish state summit at the White House appeared heavy on symbolism but light on substance, with no sign of major breakthroughs between the world’s biggest economies.

Still, Trump highlighted progress under a bilateral trade mechanism, citing what he described as increased market access for US farmers and ranchers, while both leaders identified artificial intelligence as an area for cooperation.

Trump said in remarks welcoming Xi that they would see some of the greatest treasures of US history at the National Archives, including the Declaration of Independence, the US Constitution and the Bill of Rights.

They would also see “artifacts testifying to the long and cherished relationship” between China and the United States and their “cultural exchanges”, he said.

“Just as our ancestors reached across the ocean centuries ago to trade, to learn, and to build a better world, our two countries do really the same thing, and we’re very proud of it and the relationship,” Trump said.

China has not commented on the visit to the archives, but analysts say Xi may be keen to see records relating to the US switch of recognition to communist China from Taiwan in 1979.

China presses on Taiwan

Xi has long sought to persuade Trump to state publicly that the United States opposes Taiwan’s independence, rather than saying only that it does not support independence, which has been Washington’s formulation for decades.

He is also keen to get the US to halt arms sales to the island.

As expected, Xi pressed Trump on Taiwan on Thursday, saying he hoped the United States would “handle the Taiwan question with prudence.” China’s state news agency also reported that Xi “hopes the US side will adhere to the correct position of opposing ‘Taiwan independence’.”

While the United States, like most countries, has no formal diplomatic relations with Taipei, Washington is its most important international backer and is bound by US law to provide it with the means to defend itself.

America’s Asian allies will watch closely to see how Trump talks about Taiwan following Xi’s visit.

After his May summit with Xi, Trump, whose administration in December approved an $11 billion arms sale package to Taiwan, said he was holding a second package, worth some $14bn, in abeyance and described it as a “very good negotiating chip.” Craig Singleton of the Foundation for Defence of Democracies think tank said Beijing may believe it has established a new baseline on Taiwan with Trump.

He said Xi’s use of the word “adhere” was revealing because “it implies Beijing believes Washington is already behaving in ways it wants.”

“In the context of the current stand-down on Taiwan arms sales, China may increasingly view that restraint as a new baseline rather than a temporary pause,” he said.

“Beijing’s objective is to get Trump to absorb Chinese red lines into his own definition of a stable relationship.”

On Thursday, Senate Democrats criticised the summit, saying Trump had failed to secure meaningful concessions from Beijing on trade, security, artificial intelligence or human rights.

They also criticised Trump for failing to publicly address China’s military pressure on Taiwan and called for the immediate delivery of approved military aid and arms sales to the island.

World.title: Heavy fighting, internet disruption as Ethiopia conflict rages
World.content:
Ethiopian forces battled overnight to repel an assault by Tigray rebels in the Afar region, a humanitarian source said on Friday, with reports of an internet blackout in the north of the country.

Rebels in the northern Tigray region seized local airports and launched attacks into the neighbouring states of Afar and Amhara this week, saying they were once again in a “full-blown war” with the federal government.

Locals fear a repeat of the telecoms blackout and supplies blockade imposed on Tigray during the last civil war in 2020-2022 that killed an estimated 600,000 people.

Online monitor Netblocks said there was an “internet disruption in northern Ethiopia corresponding to reports of a telecoms blackout in Tigray”.

AFP was unable to contact sources in the region by phone on Friday.

A humanitarian source in Afar said there was “heavy fighting overnight” around the town of Abala that sits in the mountains on the border with Tigray.

“The federal forces pushed the rebels from entering the town,” the source said, adding that a drone was used by the army.

Heavy clashes occurred in North Wollo Zone of Amhara on Thursday, including around the Unesco World Heritage sites in Lalibela, home to Ethiopia’s famed rock churches.

Analysts say the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) appears to be repeating its strategy from the last war — pushing south through Amhara towards the capital, Addis Ababa, while the offensive in Afar is likely aimed at cutting off supplies from Djibouti, which provides almost all of Ethiopia’s international trade cargo, including fuel.

The TPLF has forged an alliance with six other armed groups around the country in a bid to overthrow the government of Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.

“The alliance is likely trying to seize settlements alongside key infrastructure routes to undermine federal government’s ability to supply,” Edward Bach of consultancy firm Verisk Maplecroft told AFP.

The government has a significant military advantage, however, with a large arsenal of drones, an army numbering some 500,000, and the support of external actors, notably the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

The renewed fighting comes at an awkward moment for the United States, which only this month lifted sanctions on Ethiopia and Eritrea related to atrocities committed during the last civil war, saying the “national emergency… has expired”.

The US embassy sided with Ethiopia’s government this week, saying it was “disappointed to see the leadership of the TPLF… launch a large-scale offensive”.

The conflict could also draw in neighbouring Eritrea, which fears landlocked Ethiopia is planning to invade it to gain access to the Red Sea.

Panic buying

Back in Tigray, prices for basic goods have been spiking as locals raced to stock up on supplies.

“There is panic in the community,” Samuel Gebreslassie, 37, who works in a spice shop in the Tigray capital, Mekelle, told AFP on Thursday.

“There is deep fear that banks, telecom networks, electricity and basic goods could be cut off again.”

The TPLF ruled the whole of Ethiopia from 1991 to 2018 before being sidelined with Abiy’s rise, eventually triggering a civil war marked by widespread war crimes and sexual violence.

The Pretoria Peace Agreement of 2022 maintained an uneasy calm until last year, but was never fully implemented, with around one million people still displaced.

Sporadic clashes then resumed, with the federal forces launching multiple drone strikes in Tigray in recent months and massing troops at the border.

Rights groups have accused the TPLF of a campaign of forced recruitment this year as it prepared for renewed conflict.

World.title: PTI ‘still in two minds’ over march plans to Islamabad
World.content:
• Panjutha hints at possibility of postponement, links it to acceptance of party’s demands for Imran’s release, snap polls, probe into May 9 events

• PTI spox says no such proposal being discussed, insists only founder can postpone march

• Govt deploys Rangers in Islamabad, multiple districts of Punjab ahead of PTI protest

ISLAMABAD: A PTI leader on Thursday hinted at the possibility of postponing its protest march if the federal government agreed to hold elections within six to eight months, release party chief Imran Khan and other political prisoners, and investigate May 9 and November 26 crackdowns on the opposition party.

Advocate Naeem Haider Panjutha told Dawn that the protest could be postponed if these three assurances were given by the government.

There was no clarity on where such a proposal originated from, which added to confusion about the PTI’s plans for its Sept 27 protest. Party spokesperson Sheikh Waqas Akram, however, denied any such proposal was being discussed at any party forum, saying only Imran Khan could take a decision even if such a proposal was on the table.

“The first and primary condition is that the public mandate be respected and for that free, fair and tran­s­parent elections must be held within six to eight months,” Mr Panj­utha said, while demanding a clear guarantee that elections would be held before the end of this financial year.

All political prisoners, including Imran Khan, must be released — not through any deal or political settlement, but through the courts and due process of law, he said, adding that all cases against Imran Khan were “weak”.

The third demand was for a judicial inquiry into the events of May 9 and November 26. “If these three demands are fulfilled, the march can be postponed,” he said, adding that in case these demands were ignored, the PTI would be “coming with no compromise, no retreat, and no turning back”.

On the other hand, Sheikh Waqas Akram told Dawn the above mentioned conditions were shared with the government after the D-Chowk incident, but the government had not responded positively, so the conditions were then withdrawn on the order of Imran Khan. “We have not received any concrete offer from the government side, so the long march will be held come what may. Even if we get an offer, we will demand to arrange a meeting with Imran Khan, as only he can postpone it,” he added. Sheikh Waqas said the PTI cannot afford to announce postponement of march, especially when its ministers were being abducted.

In a meeting held at the opposition chamber in the Senate, PTI interim chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and former senator Mustafa Nawaz Khokhar met Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas and discussed preparations for the planned long march. According to a statement issued by the Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayeen-i-Paki­stan (TTAP), the participants held a detailed discussion on the prevailing situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and growing challenges to provincial autonomy. The meeting also focused on the Sept 27 march, preparations for the event and the strategy to be adopted in the coming days.

Rangers deployed

Separately, the federal government approved the deployment of Rangers in Islamabad and several districts of Punjab from Sept 20 to Oct 5. “Pursuant to the request made by the chief commissioner, Islamabad Capital Territory … and Home Department, government of Punjab …, the federal government is pleased to authorise deployment of sufficient strength of troops of Pakistan Rangers (Punjab) in ICT and different districts of Punjab province,” an interior ministry notification read.

The deployment has been aut­h­orised under Sections 7(b) and 10 of the Pakistan Rangers Ordin­ance, 1959, and Sections 4 and 5 of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, to perform functions specified under the laws, as authorised by the Islamabad chief commissioner or the provincial government.

“The deployed troops may respond appropriately in self-defence to any threats or violent activities encountered in the course of their duties as per rules/regulations in vogue,” the notification stated. The Punjab government also sent a letter to the interior ministry requesting mobile and internet services at specific locations in Rawalpindi and Attock to be downgraded or jam­med on Sept 27.

Published in Dawn, September 25th, 2026

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment. This should apply to Solar PV Module, Photovoltaic Cell, Solar Inverter, DC Cable, Data Logger, Aluminium Mounting Structure, Battery Pack, Battery Cell, BMS Circuit Board, PV DG Controller, Hybrid Controller, Solar Plant Safety Aluminium Walkway Mesh, Safety Accessories, and related components.

Current TTI rates are high. Solar PV Module carries 26.90 percent, Photovoltaic Cell 25.75 percent, Solar Inverter 28.73 percent, DC Cable 58.40 percent, Data Logger 37.25 percent, Aluminium Mounting Structure 58.40 percent, Battery Pack and Battery Cell 58.40 percent, BMS Circuit Board 31.50 percent, pack materials 37.25 percent, PV DG Controller or Hybrid Controller 89.08 percent, and Solar Plant Safety Aluminum Walkway Mesh 37.25 percent. These should be reduced to zero percent for renewable energy expansion.

The third reform is a tax holiday. Rooftop solar power producers and project companies should receive benefits comparable to those of utility-scale renewable energy producers. A practical structure could be a 100 percent tax holiday for the first 10 years, 50 percent for the next 3 years, and 25 percent for the next 2 years. This should apply to CAPEX, OPEX, IPP, and MPP models. A broader 10–20 year tax holiday for renewable energy projects should also be considered.

Bangladesh has a remarkable solar opportunity already waiting on its rooftops. About 7 percent of the country’s land is covered with concrete or other built structures. This means more than 10,000 square kilometres, or about 10 billion square meters of built surface. If only 30 percent is usable, that would give around 3 billion square meters. At 10 square meters per kW, this can create nearly 300 GW of solar potential. Bangladesh’s peak demand is only around 16–18 GW. The opportunity already exists on rooftops, factories, warehouses, schools, hospitals, government buildings, and commercial establishments.

Rooftop solar should therefore be relaunched nationwide with a clear business model. Utility-scale solar also needs support through unused khas land, transparent tendering, and grid readiness. Floating solar, river-based solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage should receive separate policy attention.

The suspended solar projects must also be revisited. A total of 31 solar power projects, with a combined capacity of more than 3,000 MW, were previously suspended or cancelled. Many were being developed by foreign investors, with more than USD 200 million reportedly already invested. If implemented, these projects could save around BDT 10,800 crore annually in energy import costs. They should be reassessed and revived quickly.

Energy storage is another missing pillar. Solar and wind need storage support to become more reliable. Duties on lithium-ion batteries, BESS, and other storage systems should be reduced to zero. This will help stabilise renewable power and support future grid flexibility.

Electric vehicles can also become part of the solution. In China, Japan, and the United States, EVs are increasingly seen as mobile energy storage systems.
